Med. 660 ; ἀ. βίβλινον (sc. οἶνον) tap it, Theoc. 14.15 ; γῆρυν ἀνοίξας, for στόμα, Tryph. 477 ; ἀ. φιλήματα kiss with open mouths, Ach.Tat. 2.37.
throw open for use, γυμνάσιον OGI 529.11 ; κἀνῷξε σχολὰς opened school, Phld. Acad. Ind. p. 103M. ; εἰ ἀνοίξω ἐργαστήριον; shall I open a shop? Astramps. Orac. 43 p. 5H. metaph, lay open, unfold, disclose, ὄνομα A. Supp. 322 ; ἔργ’ ἀναιδῆ S. OC 515, cf. E. IA 326 ; λανθάνουσαν ἀτυχίαν Men. 674. as nautical term, abs., get into the open sea, get clear of land, X. HG 1.1.2, 5.13, 6.21 ; but ἁλὸς κέλευθον ἀ. Pi. P. 5.88 is to open or first show the way over the sea. Pass., to be open, stand open, lie open, ὄπισθε τῆς ἀνοιγομένης θύρης Hdt. 1.9 ; ἀνεῳγμένην καταλαμβάνειν τὴν θύραν Pl. Smp. 174e ; ἀνεῳγμένας πύλας ᾍδου E. Hipp. 56 ; δικαστήρια ἀνοίγεται Pl. R. 405a ; παρέξει τἀμπόρι’ ἀνεῳγμένα Ar. Av. 1523 ; ἀνέῳκται τὸ δεσμωτήριον D. 24.208 ; λέων τὰ ἐντὸς ἀνοιχθείς cut open, Arist. HA 497b17 ; κόλποι δι’ ἀλλήλων ἀνοιγόμενοι opening one into another, Plu. Crass. 4 ; metaph, θησαυρὸς ὡς ἀνοίγνυται κακῶν E. Ion 923.
v. ἀνοίγνυμι.

blow up, inflate, Poll. 4.179 ; aor. inf. ἀνοιδῆναι QS. 14.470.
intr., = ἀνοιδέω, Nic. Fr. 68.7.
εως, ἡ, = ἀνοίδησις, dilatation, opp. συστολή, Plot. 4.5.7 (pl.).
Ep. ἀνοιδέω.

Ep. ἀνοιδείω Nic. Th. 855 ; fut. -ήσω ; aor. ἀνῴδησα E. Hipp. 1210, Pl. Ti. 84e ; pf. ἀνῴδηκα Hp. Acut. 10 : — swell up, Hp. l.c. ; of a wave, E. l.c., cf. Alciphr. 1.10 ; of wind in the body, Pl. l.c. ; of figs ripening, Nic. l.c. ; τὰ στέρνα ἀνῴδει Aeschin. Ep. 1.2 ; τὸ κάλυμμα ἀνῳδηκός swollen out, inflated, Arist. HA 625a2, cf. GA 728b28. metaph, θυμὸς ἀνοιδέει Hdt. 7.39 ; ὀργαῖς… ἀνοιδούσαις Phld. Ir. p. 63 W. ; of anger, ἀνοιδήσας ὁ βασιλεύς Philostr. VA 7.33 (so in Med., θυμὸν ἀνοιδήσαντο they swelled with rage, QS. 9.345) ; ἀνοιδούσης τῆς νόσου Philostr. VA 4.4.
εως, ἡ, swelling, intumescence, τῶν μαστῶν Arist. HA 574b16, al. ; θαλάσσης Id. Mu. 399a27 (pl.).
make to swell, σῖτον Thphr. CP 4.13.7 ; — Pass., = ἀνοιδέω, Hp. Acut. 10.

ον, not of the family, S.E. P. 1.67 ; Comp. -ότερος less closely related, Phlp. in Ph. 256.14.
unfitting, unseasonable, Cic. Att. 16.11.4, DS. 3.56, Plu. 2.102a ; c. gen., foreign to, incongruous with, Epicur. Ep. 3 p. 60U., Plb. 6.10.1, 24.5.13, DS. 12.21 ; c. dat., dissimilar to, Plb. 5.96.8 ; alien from, κενοδοξίᾳ Porph. Antr. 4 (Sup.) ; abs., Phld. Po. 1676.9, Id. D. 3.8 (Comp.). Adv. -ως, ῥηθῆναι Simp. in Ph. 350.27.
Astrol., not in its domicile, Vett.Val. 50.2. Adv. -ως Id. 44.5.

ητος, ἡ, ineptitude, Eustr. in EN 364.18.
incongruity, Iamb. Myst. 1.4.
ον, not to be adapted, alien, ἀλλήλοις M.Ant 12.30.
παρὰ τὸ εἰκὸς εἰρημένον, EM 110.55, cf. Hsch. s.v. ἀνοκηδεολόγον.
ον, = ἀοίκητος, Hdt. 4.31.

remove up the country, ἀ. τὴν Σπάρτην, i.e. break it up as a city, Arist. Rh. Al. 1423a7 ; ἀ. τινὰς ἐς τὴν Περσίδα Paus. 1.25.5, cf. Str. 13.3.3 ; ἀ. [τέττιγας] φθόνου ἐς δένδρα remove them out of envy΄s way, dub. in Philostr. VA 7.11 (leg. ἀπ-) ; — Pass. and Med., shift one΄s dwelling up the country, migrate inland or to higher ground, αὐτοὶ δ’ ἀνῳκίσανθ’ ὅπως ἀνωτάτω Ar. Pax 207, cf. Av. 1351, Str. 9.2.17, App. Pun. 84 ; and of cities, to be built inland or away from the coast, Th. 1.7 ; — generally, migrate, ἀνοικίσασθαι εἰς Ὄλυνθον Id. 1.58, cf. 8.31.
resettle, colonize afresh, Paus. 2.1.2, Memn. 60 (Med.) ; rebuild, Aps. pp. 239, 245 H. ; — Pass., to be repeopled, Plu. Luc. 29.
εως, ἡ, shifting people upward and inland, App. Pun. 84.

ὁ, = ἀνοίκισις, Str. 9.2.17, prob. in Ph. 2.526.
rebuilding, restoration, πόλεων Hdn. 3.6.9.
ον, Astrol., without a dominant planet, Vett.Val. 134.17, 151.5.

build up, τὰ χείλεα τοῦ ποταμοῦ… ἀνοικοδόμηδε πλίνθοισι Hdt. 1.186.
wall up, λαύρας καιναῖς πλίνθοισιν ἀ. Ar. Pax 100 ; θύραν Lycurg. 128 ; πύλας dub.l. in DS. 11.21 (in this sense ἀποικ- is a freq.v.l.).
build again, rebuild, πόλιν καὶ τείχη Th. 1.89, cf. Jusj. ap. Lycurg. 81, X. HG 4.44.19, etc. ; ἀ. χώραν occupy again with buildings, DS. 15.66 ; — Pass., metaph, to be exalted, LXX Ma. 3.15.
ἡ, rebuilding, restoration, PLond. 2.216.18 (i AD), PAmh. 93.19 (ii AD) ; Dor. ἀνοικοδομά IG 12(1).9 (Rhodes).
εως, ἡ, = ἀνοικοδομή, Arist. Ath. 23.4.
ἡ, building up, IG 4.823.6 (Troezen), Sch. Th. 8.90.

ον, not set in order, unarranged, Macho ap. Ath. 8.341b, Longin. 33.5.
Act., managing badly, Plu. 2.517e, v.l. in Gell. 12.12.4.
ον, houseless, homeless, ἄ. ποιέειν τινά Hdt. 3.145 ; cf. ἄοικος.
or ἀνοικτί, Adv. = ἀνοίκτως, Hdn. Epim. 257.
one must open, E. Ion 1387.
ἀταλαιπώρητον, Hsch.
ου, ὁ, one who opens, ADysc. Synt. 324.6.
= ἀνοικτεί.
ή, όν, fit for opening, Lyd. Mens. 4.64 ; ἀνοικτικόν means of opening the mouth, Orib. Fr. 48.
ον, gen. ονος, pitiless, merciless, S. Fr. 659.8, AP 7.303 (Antip.Sid.).
ον, unmourned, σῶμα [Arist.] Pepl. 28. Act., pitiless, Περσεφόνης θάλαμοι IG 2.3765 (Supp. p. 283). Adv. -τως Antipho 1.25.
ή, όν, capable of being opened, Babr. 59.11, Luc. VH 1.24.
ον, pitiless, ruthless, E. Tr. 787, Ar. Th. 1022. Adv. -τως without pity, without being pitied, S. OT 180, E. Tr. 756 ; also ἀνοίκτρως Ant.Lib. 39 (s.v.l.).
= ἀνοίκτως, v. ἄνοικτος.
wail aloud, A. Pers. 465, Th. 3.113, Telecl. 1 D.
Adv. without need to wail, with impunity, S. Aj. 1227 ; without wailing, Philostr.Jun. Im. 10.
ον, unmourned, unlamented, A. Ch. 433, 511.
ον, = ἄοινος, Hdn. Epim. 216.

εως, ἡ, opening, πυλῶν Th. 4.67, 68 ; πόρων Thphr. Od. 13 ; χειλῶν Plu. 2.738c, cf. PMagLond. 46.274 (iv AD) ; pl., Porph. Antr. 27 ; ἄ. τοῦ στόματος, Hebraism for παρρησία, LXX Ez. 29.21, 2 Ep. Cor. 6.11, Ep. Eph. 6.19, etc.
εως, ἡ, (< ἀναφέρω, ἀνοίσω) bringing back, Suid.
one must carry back or report, S. Ant. 272, E. HF 1221 : — one must refer, τι πρός τι Plu. Phoc. 5 ; ἐπί τι Thphr. CP 4.11.8.
α, ον, to be referred, E. Fr. 970.
*ἀνοιστός, ή, όν, brought back, ἀ. ἔς τινα referred to some one for decision, Hdt. 6.66 (v.l. ἀνωΐστου).
goad to madness, E. Ba. 979 ; ἔρωτι καρδίην ἀνοιστρηθείς Herod. 1.57.
v. ἀναφέρω.
v. ἄνω.
ὑπερῷον, γράφεται καὶ ἀνώγεων, Hsch.
v. ἀνοικῆ.
Adv. = ἀόκνως, POxy. 743.39 (i BC), PFay. 130.14 (iii AD).

Ion. ἀνακ-, hold back, stay, hinder, ἀ. τὰς νέας keep them riding at anchor, Hdt. 6.116 (cf. Hsch. s.v. ἀνακωχεύω), etc. ; metaph, of a chariot, hold it in, keep it back, S. El. 732 ; also ἀ. πόλεμον DH. 9.16. ἀ. τὸν τόνον τῶν ὅπλων keep up the tension of the ropes, keep them taut, Hdt. 7.36.
keep afloat, Arist. Cael. 313a23. also intr. (sc. ἑαυτόν), keep still, Hdt. 9.13 ; hold back, of ships, DS. 11.18. — The form ἀνακωχέω support, relieve strain upon, is found in Hp. Art. 9, 38, Mochl. 2.

ἡ, redupl. form = ἀνοχή (cf. ὄκωχα pf. of ἔχω), stay, cessation, κακῶν Th. 4.117 ; ἀ. νομῆς a stay in the spreading of the ulcer, Aret. SD 2.9, cf. 1.8. esp. cessation of arms, truce, δι’ ἀνοκωχῆς γίγνεσθαί τινι to be at truce with one, Th. 1.40 ; ἀ. ἐστί τινι πρός τινα one party has a truce with another, Id. 5.32.
hindrance, τριβὴ καὶ ἀ. τῶν Ἐλλήνων Id. 8.87.
(Archaic word used by Th. acc. to DH. Amm. 2.3. Mss. generally have the corrupt form ἀνακωχή, which gave rise to a deriv. παρὰ τὸ ἄνω τὰς ἀκωκὰς ἔχειν EM 96.52 ; but Hsch. gives the correct form. Ammon. Diff. 19 attempts to distinguish the forms.)
εως, ἡ, glossed by σύμπτωσις, Bacch. ap. Erot. s.v. (ἀνακώχησις codd.).
to be ἄνολβος, Epic.Oxy. 1794.13.
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, the state of an ἄνολβος, misery, Hes. Op. 319 [ι].
ον, = ἄνολβος, v.l. in Hdt. 1.32.

ον, poet. Adj. unblest, wretched, luckless, ἦμαρ Orac. ap. Hdt. 1.85 ; γαῖα, ὄμμα, E. Hel. 247, IA 354 ; ὤμοι ἐμῶν ἄνολβα βουλευμάτων, for ἐμὰ… βουλεύματα, S. Ant. 1265 ; of persons, Thgn. 288 (Comp.), A. Eu. 551, S. Aj. 1156, etc.
without means, poor, Arat. 1073.
ον, not ruined, having escaped ruin, Il. 13.761.
aor. -ώλισθον, slip or glide back, return, ἔς τινα Call. Fr. 96.
ἡ, hauling up, λίθων Th. 4.112 ; ἀ. καὶ καθολκή Aen.Tact. 10.12.

cry aloud, shout aloud, ἀνωλόλυξα χαρᾶς ὕπο A. Ag. 587, cf. Simon. 148.2, S. Tr. 205, E. Med. 1173, etc. c. acc., bewail loudly, S. El. 750 ; but c. acc. cogn., βοὴν ἀ. E. Tr. 1000. causal, excite by Bacchic cries, πρώτας δὲ Θήβας… ἀνωλόλυξα Id. Ba. 24.
bewail aloud, Th. 8.81, X. Cyr. 7.3.14, J. AJ 2.6.4 ; c. part., ἀ. ποθῶν… Pl. Prt. 327d.
ἀδάκρυτον, Hsch. (ἀνωλόφυκτον cod.).
άδος, ἡ, an Olympiad omitted in the list, Paus. 6.22.3.
v. ἄνω.
restore to equality, equalize, Pass., pf. inf. ἀνωμαλίσθαι Arist. Rh. 1412a16 ; fut., cj. in Pol. 1265a40 ; cf. ἀνομάλωσις.
εως, ἡ, restoration of equality, equalization, ib. 1274b9.
gush out with water, πηγή Ph. 2.91 ; metaph, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ γῆς τῆς αἰσθήσεως ἀνομβρησάντων παθῶν 1.575 ; c. acc., Pour forth, ὕδωρ 2.115 ; metaph, LXX Si. 18.29, al., Ph. 1.477.
εσσα, εν, rainy, Nic. Al. 288.
ἡ, want of rain, Arist. HA 606b20, DS. 1.29, J. AJ 8.13.2, Ph. 2.383 ; metaph, [τὴν παίδευσιν] οὔτε ὄμβρος οὔτε ἀ. ἀφαιρεῖται Antipho Soph. 60.
ον, without rain, of countries, Hdt. 2.22, 4.185. ἄ. ῥοαί streams not fed by showers, E. Ba. 406.
to be ἄνομος, act lawlessly, περὶ τὸ ἱρόν Hdt. 1.144. Pass., to be unlawfully used, POxy. 1465.9 (i BC).
ον, of unlike age, Procl. in Prm. p. 949S.
ατος, τό, transgression of the law, Lys. ap. Phot. p. 143 R., LXX Le. 20.14, al., Stoic. 3.136, DS. 17.5.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, lawlessness, lawless conduct, opp. δικαιοσύνη, Hdt. 1.96, 97 ; ἀ. νόμων κρατεῖ E. IA 1095 (lyr.) ; ἀ. ἀμύνειν Antipho 4.1.7 ; ἀ. ὀφλισκάνειν E. Ion 443 ; ἀντὶ αὐτονομίας… εἰς ἀνομίας ἐμπίπτειν Isoc. 6.64, cf. Plu. 2.755b ; ζῆν ἐν πάσῃ ἀναρχίᾳ καὶ ἀ. Pl. R. 575a.
the negation of law, opp. νόμος, D. 24.152.

ον, having no communion with others, unsociable, Pl. Lg. 951a, Plu. 2.50b, etc. c. gen., ἀ. παιδείας uneducated, Pl. Ep. 332c ; abs., Luc. Merc. Cond. 14 ; c. dat., ἀ. τοῖς ἔργοις τῆς τέχνης Gal. 15.159, 18(1).287.
ον, v.l. for ἄνομος, Pl. Min. 314d.
ον, not customary, Orac. ap. Phleg. Mir. 10.
ον, without mist, ἀήρ Arist. Mu. 394a23.
ον, eyeless, sightless, S. Ph. 856 (lyr.), Orph. Fr. 82.
ἡ, difference in kind, Epicur. Fr. 36.
ές, of different kind, ibid. (prob.), Chrysipp. Stoic. 2.81, Arr. Epict. 1.20.2, Alex.Aphr. in Top. 116.10, al., S.E. M. 8.229.
ές, differing in species, Plot. 4.3.2, Iamb. Myst. 1.19, Dam. Pr. 34 ; v.l. for ἀνόμοιο-, Arist. EN 1163b32. Adv. -ειδῶς Dam. Pr. 37.
ον, having a different bent, S.E. M. 7.56.
ον, unregulated by law, Pl. Lg. 781a, 785a, Arist. Pol. 1269b19 ; ἄγραφον καὶ ἀ. φύσεως δίκαιον DH. 7.41.
ές, of unevenly distributed weight, Arist. Cael. 273b23.
ές, of different kind, Ph. 2.307. Adv. -νῶς in a different gender, Sch. rec. S. Ant. 74.
ον, with dissimilar angles, Papp. 216.20.
ἡ, v. ἀνομοιοειδής.
ές, of unlike kind, heterogeneous, φιλίαι Arist. EN 1163b32, cf. Dam. Pr. 440 ; — hence Subst. ἀνομοιοείδεια, ἡ, ADysc. Pron. 101.22.
ον, with different terminations, ADysc. Synt. 167.25.

ές, consisting of unlike parts, not homogeneous, esp. of organs, opp. tissues, Arist. HA 486a7, Mete. 388a18, GA 722b31, Thphr. Fr. 22, Gal. 6.844, al. in Metric, [συστήματα] κατὰ περικοπὴν ἀνομοιομερῆ Heph. Poëm. 4.
όν, causing unlikeness, Dam. Pr. 342.
ον, with unlike inflexions, Eust. 1228.62. Adv. -τως Id. 631.27.

ον, Pl. Phlb. 13e, etc., also α, ον Isoc. 12.225, etc. : — unlike, dissimilar, Pi. N. 8.28 ; ἀ. τινι unlike it, Pl. Grg. 513b, al. ; ἐξ ἀνομοίων ἡ πόλις is composed of dissimilar elements, Arist. Pol. 1277a5. Adv. -ως Th. 1.84, Pl. R. 388c, al. ; ἀ. ἔχειν X. An. 7.7.49.
of number, = ἑτερομήκης, Theol.Ar. 9, 58.
ον, consisting of unequal strophes, Heph. Poëm. 5.3.
ον, gen. ονος, of unlike form, Gal. 18(1).774, Procl. Inst. 210, Phlp. in Ph. 677.2.
ητος, ἡ, unlikeness, dissimilarity, Pl. Prm. 159e, Plt. 273d, Thphr. CP 1.2.2, Hierocl. in CA 26 p. 481M. ; in pl., Pl. Plt. 294, Arist. Po. 1448a10.
ον, differing in modality (including quantity and quality, πρότασις Eustr. in APo. 52.17.
ον, of different kind, Sm. Le. 19.19.
ον, in Metric, of dissimilar quantity, Eust. 13.7.
ουν, of different colour, Alex.Aphr. de An. 146.8.

(< ἀνόμοιος) make unlike or dissimilar, Pl. R. 546b, Prm. 148b ; — Pass. (c. fut. Med., Porph. Abst. 1.37), to be or become so, Pl. Tht. 166b, al.
(< ἀνά, ὁμοιόω) make even again, PHal. 1.100 (iii BC).
ες, unlike, Procl. Inst. 203.
εως, ἡ, a making unlike, dissimilarity, Pl. Tht. 166c.

agree upon a thing, come to an understanding, περί τινος Pl. R. 442e ; πρὸς ἀλλήλους ib. 348b ; πρός τι with a view to…, Id. Tht. 164c ; τινί with a person, Plu. 2.1070d (Act. in codd.) ; abs., admit, Muson. Fr. 17 p. 92H., Sammelb. 4638.14.
recapitulate, sum up one΄s conclusions, τὰ εἰρημένα Pl. Smp. 200e.
pay money by note of hand or order, Lys. ap. Phot. p. 143 R., IG 1.188.34. Act., in later Prose, ἀ. τινί Plu. 2.1070d codd. ; D. 18.86 uses the pf. in pass. sense, ἀνωμολόγημαι… τὰ ἄριστα πράττειν I am allowed by all to have done what is best, cf. ib. 266, 60.4, and late Prose, Ph. 1.161, al. ; aor. part. Pass. -ηθείς 2.520.
ατος, τό, promissory note, ib. 17.
one must admit, τοῦτο περὶ αὐτῶν Pl. R. 452e, cf. Lg. 737c.
ον, agreed on again, under a renewed bill for both the principal debt and the unpaid interest, AB 211. (ἀ- priv.) inconsistent, τὸ ἀ. Ptol. Tetr. 47.

ἡ, verbal agreement, Hsch. (< ἀνομόλογος) disagreement, Str. 2.3.3, Plu. Comp. Nic. Crass. 1.
failure to lead a consistent life, title of treatise by Chrysipp., Stoic. 3.94, cf. Posidon. ib. 112 ; generally, inconsistency, Hierocl. p. 56A.
ον, not agreeing, incongruous, S.E. M. 8.331, cf. Harp. s.v. ἀσυνθετώτατον, Apollon.Cit. 3 ; c. dat., Alex.Aphr. in Top. 548.17. Adv. -γως Porph. Abst. 2.40.

η, ον, not agreeing, inconsistent, ἵνα μὴ ἀ. ἦ ὁ λόγος Pl. Grg. 495a ; ἀ. τοῖς προειρημένοις Arist. APr. 48a21, cf. Chrysipp. Stoic. 3.125.
not admitted, not granted, τὰ ἀνομολογούμενα συνάγειν Arist. Rh. 1396b28, cf. 1400a15 ; — Adj., compd. of ἀ- priv. and ὁμολογούμενος; for a Verb ἀνομολογέομαι, disagree with, does not occur. Adv. -νως Gal. 5.470.
ον, differing in οὐσία, Ps-Alex.Aphr. in SE 12.17.
ον, (νόμος II) unmusical, νόμος ἄ. A. Ag. 1142 (lyr.).

ον, lawless, impious, τράπεζα Hdt. 1.162 ; of persons, S. OC 142, al. ; στρατός Tr. 1096 ; Ἐχίονος γόνος E. Ba. 995 ; of things, θυσία A. Ag. 151 ; πάθη E. Or. 1455 ; μοναρχία Pl. Plt. 302e ; τὰ ἄνομα lawless acts, Hdt. 1.8 ; Comp. -ώτερος Pl. Hp. Ma. 285a. Adv. -μως E. Med. 1000, Antipho 4.1.2, Th. 4.92. c. gen., ἀ. θεοῦ, i.e. without (the Mosaic) Law and therefore without God, 1 Ep. Cor. 9.21. Adv. ἀνόμως, = χωρὶς νόμου, Ep. Rom. 2.12.
illegal, κατοχή POxy. 237 vii 11 (ii AD).
ον, contradictory, PHib. 31.4.15.
ές, of a different order, Dam. Pr. 119 ; not co-ordinated, of lines of vision, prob. l. in Gal. UP 10.12 ; cf. ὁμοταγής.
ον, differing in substance, Phlp. in de An. 526.18.
Dor. for ἀνόνητος.
ἄνωθεν, Hsch. (fort. ἀνοκόνδως, cf. ἀνάκανδα).
ον, irreproachable, Nic.Dam. p. 119D.

Dor. ἀνόνατος, ον, unprofitable, περισσὰ κἀνόνητα σώματα S. Aj. 758 ; ὦπολλὰ λέξας… κἀνόνητ’ ἔπη v.l. ib. 1272 ; ἀ. γάμος E. Or. 1501 (lyr.), cf. Hel. 886 ; ἀ. γίγνεσθαι D. 9.40, cf. Plu. 2.248a ; τινί Arist. EN 1095a9, cf. Pol. 1334b40 ; ἄργυρον εἰς ἀνόνατα ῥέοντα Cerc. 4.4 ; — neut. pl. ἀνόνητα is freq. in E. as Adv., in vain, as Hec. 766, Alc. 412 (lyr.), al. ; ἀνόνητα πονεῖν Pl. R. 486c ; regul. Adv. -τως Pall. in Hp. 2.147D, Sch. E. Or. 1501 ; Comp., ibid.
Act., c. gen., τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀ. τινα ποιῆσαι deprive of all benefit from…, D. 18.141, cf. 19.315, Plu. 2.800d, Nic.Dam. p. 13D.
ον, faulty form for ἀνωνόμαστος, Gal. 7.425, Hdn. Epim. 203, Suid.
ον, not to be written with the acute accent, Eust. 930.57.

ον, contr. ἄνους, ουν, without understanding, silly, κραδίη Il. 21.441 ; ψυχή Pl. Ti. 44a, etc. ; of persons, S. Ant. 99 ; ἄνους τε καὶ γέρων ἅμα ib. 281 ; πλοῦτος ἄ. wealth without wit, AP 9.43 (Parmen.) ; Comp. ἀνούστερος A. Pr. 987 ; Sup. ἀνούστατος Pherecr. 19D. Adv., Comp. ἀνουστέρως S. Fr. 589.1.

only in Od. 1.320 ὄρνις δ’ ὣς ἀνοπαῖα διέπτατο, where it is variously written and explained ; acc. to Hdn. Gr. 2.133, it is an Adv. (compd. of ἀνά, ὄπτομαι), she flew away unseen, unnoticed ; or, acc. to Eust., = ἄνω, ἀνωφερές, up into the air, cf. καρπαλίμως ἀνόπαιον Emp. 51, and Ἀνόπαια, the name of the pass above Thermopylae (Hdt. 7.216). acc. to Aristarch., ἀνόπαια or πανόπαια, a kind of eagle, cf. Hebr. ΄ănāphā ΄heron΄. acc. to Gramm. in An.Ox. 1.83, ἀν’ ὀπαῖα (= ἀνὰ ὀπήν) up by the hole in the roof, up the smoke-vent.
Adv. backwards, Hsch. ; farther back, in a book. etc., Eust. 1031.46.

ον, without the ὅπλον or large shield, of the Persians, who bore only γέρρα, Hdt. 9.62 ; generally, unarmed, Pl Euthd. 299b, Onos. 42.17 ; τὸ ἄ., opp. τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, of citizens not entrusted with arms, Arist. Pol. 1289b32 ; — of ships, unarmed, Plb. 2.12.3. (On the form v. ἄοπλος.)
ον, unseen, Suid.
ον, v.l. for ἀόρ- in Pl. Ti. 51a, Polycharm. 1.

lit. knead up ; in Pass., ἀνωργασμένον σῶμα relaxed, Hp. Int. 21.
toss, dandle, παιδία Hsch. (nisi ad ἀνορταλίζειν spectat).
ον, without instruments, Plu. Per. 16 ; βίος Porph. Abst. 1.6 ; κίνησις ἀ. monement without limbs for the purpose, of serpents, Plu. 2.381b.
ον, Hellenistic for ἄνοργος, Moer. 12, cf. Sch. Pi. P. 10.33.
ἡ, = ἀμυησία, Hsch., Suid.

ον, not celebrated with orgies, ἱερά Ar. Lys. 898 ; τελεταί, i.e. no true mysteries, Ph. 1.156. of a god or person in whose honour no orgies are held, Pl. Epin. 985d.
uninitiated, Ph. 2.268 ; ἀμύητος καὶ ἀ. τῶν ἱερῶν Them. Or. 13.166c.
ον, not wrathful, Cratin. 385.
ἡ, more common in Ion. form ἠνορέη, Pi. O. 8.67, al., Theoc. 29.19.
hand up, of the elephant΄s use of his trunk, Arist. HA 497b28.
have no appetite, Antyll. ap. Orib. 5.29.8, Sor. 2.43.

ον, without appetite for, ἀπολαύσεως Arist. VV 1250b9 ; ἡδονῆς Andronic. Rhod. p. 576 M. ; περὶ τὰς ἀπολαύσεις Arist. VV 1250a8 ; abs., Sor. 1.24, Plu. 2.460a, etc. Adv. ἀνορέκτως, ἔχειν Gal. 10.576. Pass., not desired, of food, Plu. 2.664a.
ἡ, want of desire or appetite, Ti.Locr. 102e, Aret. CA 2.3.
α, ον, (ἀνήρ) = ἀνδρεῖος, πόλεμος S. Fr. 436.

call out, shout aloud, And. 1.29.
prick up, τὰ ὦτα Ph. 2.188, al. ; — Pass., ἐγήγερται καὶ ἀνωρθίασται 1.381.
ον, (ἀ- priv.) perh. sloping, ἄ. εἰς τὸ εἴσω IG2². 463.60 ; prob. corrupt in Herophil. ap. Gal. 2.571.

aor. ἀνώρθωσα E. Alc. 1138, Isoc. 5.64, etc. ; plpf. with double augm. ἠνωρθώκει v.l. in Lib. Ep. 1039 ; the double augm. is common in the compd. ἐπανορθόω : — set up again, restore, rebuild, τὸν νηόν Hdt. 1.19 ; τὸ τεῖχος 7.208 ; τὸ στρατόπεδον Th. 6.88, etc. ; τὸ σῶμά τινος E. Ba. 364 ; — Med., ἀνορθοῦσθαι τὰ πίπτοντα τῶν οἰκοδομημάτων have them rebuilt, Arist. Pol. 1322b20.
restore to health or well being, πόλιν S. OT 46 ; τινά Pl. Lg. 919d.
set straight again, set right, correct, τινά E. Supp. 1228 ; τὰ ἀλλότρια κακά Pl. R. 346e.
εως, ἡ, restoration, τειχῶν PRyl. 157.13 (ii AD) ; = ἐπανόρθωσις, Ph. Fr. 54 H. ; f.l. in Plb. 15.20.5, Corn. ND 16.
Aeol. impf. ὀννώριν<ν>ε, stir up, arouse, (sc. παφλάσμους) Alc. Supp. 25.8.
ον, bound by no oath, Poll. 1.39.
Pass., startup, try eagerly to do a thing, c. acc. cogn., στόλον Oppian. H. 3.105. — Hsch. has the Act. in neut. signf., and so Ruf. ap. Orib. 45.30.40, mount, of a disease.
Adv. with an upward rush, Sch. Oppian. H. 5.210.
ον, impetuous, Erot. s.v. ἀνάσσυτος.
take [ships] from their moorings, ἐς τὸ πέλαγος τὰς ναῦς DC. 48.48 ; — Med., put to sea, Id. 42.7 ; — Pass., anchor above, ὑπὲρ τόπον Id. 71.2.
ον, without harbour, πέτραι Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. λισσάδας πέτρας ; metaph, ὑμέναιον ὃν δόμοις ἄνορμον εἰσέπλευσας S. OT 423.
νοῦς, Scythian word, Hsch., cf. Hdn. Epim. 240.

fut. -όρσω, rouse, stir up, ἀνὰ μὲν φόρμιγγ΄, ἀνὰ δ’ αὐλὸν ὄρσομεν Pi. N. 9.8 ; τινά ARh. 4.1352 ; — Pass., ἂν δ’ ἄρα Τυδεΐδης ὦρτο (Ep. aor.) up he started, Il. 23.812, cf. Od. 8.3 ; ἀνὰ δ’ ὤρνυτ’ Ἰήσων ARh. 1.349.

poet. Verb, used by Hom. only in aor.1 (X. Eq. 3.7, 8.5 has pres. inf. and part.) : — start up, leap up, abs., Il. 9.193, Od. 3.149, Sappho Supp. 20a. 11, etc. ; ἐκ δὲ θρόνων ἀνόρουσαν Od. 22.23 ; ἐξ ὕπνοιο μάλα κραιπνῶς ἀ. Il. 10.162, etc. ; ἐς δίφρον δ’ ἀ. 11.273 ; so Ἠέλιος δ’ ἀνόρουσε… οὐρανὸν ἐς… Helios went swiftly up the sky, Od. 3.1 ; τοῖσι δὲ Νέστωρ ἡδυεπὴς ἀ. Il. 1.248 ; ἀνορούσαις (Aeol. part.) Pi. O. 7.37.
ον, roofless, πέτρα E. Ba. 38.
ον, without rump, καρκίνος Arist. HA 525b31 ; πτῆσις ἀ. without help from the tail or rump, of insects, ib. 532a24.
clap the wings and crow, like a cock, Ar. Eq. 1344.
ον, not obtained by digging, ἅλες Orib. Eup. 4.24.

Att. ἀνορύττω, pf. Pass. ἀνορώρυγμαι Men. 468 : — dig up what has been buried, τὰ ὀστέα Hdt. 2.41, Lycurg. 113 ; ὑδρίας Ar. Av. 602 ; τινά Id. Pax 372, Plu. Ages. 20 ; χρυσόν Luc. Cont. 11. ἀ. τάφον dig up, break open, destroy it, Hdt. 1.68, Isoc. 16.26.
leap up and dance, E. Supp. 719 ; of the soul, Ph. 1.379.

ον, without testicles, i.e. castrated, Hp. Vict. 2.49.
without stones, φοίνικες. Arist. Fr. 267.
ὀλιγόρρυτον ὕδωρ, Hsch.
ον, untended, S. Fr. 264.
ον, without sickness, S. Fr. 1014, PIand. 13.11 (in AD).
ἡ, (ἀ- priv., νόσος) fredom from sickness, Poll. 3.107.
ἡ, (ἀ- priv., ὅσιος) ἀνοσίhα ϝοι γένοιτυ may he be accursed, Inscr.Cypr. 135.29 H. (perh. neut. pl. ἀνόσιhα) ; cf. ἀνόσιος.

ον, more rarely α, ον E. Tr. 1316 (lyr.), Aeschin. 2.157 (dub.), and later : — unholy, profane, opp. ἄδικος, as ὅσιος to δίκαιος (v. ὅσιος I. 1), of persons, A. Th. 611, S. OT 353, etc. ; ἀ. ὁ θεομισής Pl. Euthphr. 7a ; ἄδικος καὶ ἀ. Id. Grg. 505b. of things, ἔργον, μόρος, στόμα, etc., Hdt. 2.114, 3.65, S. OC 981, etc. ; αὐδῶν ἀνόσι’ οὐδὲ ῥητά μοι Id. OT 1289 ; ἀνόσια πάσχειν Antipho 2.4.7 ; ἀσεβὲς μηδὲν μηδὲ ἀ. X. Cyr. 8.7.22 ; οὐ μόνον ἄνομον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀ. Id. Lac. 8.5 ; ἀ. νέκυς a corpse with all the rites unpaid, S. Ant. 1071 ; ἀ. τι γεγένηται ἐμοῦ παρόντος the holy rites have been profaned, Antipho 5.84. Adv. -ίως in unholy wise, S. Ph. 257 ; κάτω γῆς ἀ. οἰκῶν without funeral rites, or through an unholy deed, E. El. 677.
ητος, ἡ, unholiness, wickedness, v.l. in Pl. Euthphr. 5d ; ἀ. καὶ δεινότης τῶν πεπραγμένων Isoc. 12.121.
act impiously, wickedly, Pl. Lg. 905b, Ph. 2.128, DC. 56.5, 77.12.
ατος, τό, impious act, Ph. 2.313, Porph. Chr. 58.
ἡ, impiety, wickedness, Pl. Ep. 335b, Plu. Arat. 54, DC. 71.30.
όν, acting impiously, Pl. Ep. 352c, Arist. EN 1166b5, Ph. 2.313.
ον, = ἄνοδμος, without smell, v.l. in Hp. Acut. 63, cf. Arist. HA 634b19, etc. ; ἴχνη ἄνοσμα footsteps that leave no scent, Poll. 5.12 ; — but ἄοσμος was preferred.

Ion. and Ep. ἄνουσος, ον, without sickness, healthy, sound, of persons, ἀσκηθέες καὶ ἄ. Od. 14.255 ; ἄ. καὶ ἀγήραοι Pi. Fr. 143, cf. Pl. Ti. 33a ; ἄπηρος, ἄ. Hdt. 1.32 ; λῶστον δὲ τὸ ζῆν ἄ. S. Fr. 356. Adv. ἀνόσως, διάγειν Hp. Epid. 1.1 ; ζῆν Ph. 1.267 ; ἄ. ᾤχετ’ ἐς ἡμιθέους IG 5(2).472.13 (Megalopolis, ii/iii AD). c. gen., ἄ. κακῶν untouchid by ill, E. IA 982 ; ἄ. πρὸς τὰ ἄλλα ἀρρωστήματα, τῶν ἄλλων ἀρρωστημάτων, Arist. HA 604a12, 22. of a season, free from sickness, ἔτος ἄ. ἐς τὰς ἄλλας ἀσθενείας Th. 2.49 ; ἕξις, λόγος ἄ., Plu. Cic. 8, 2.7b. of things, not causing disease, harmless, E. Ion 1201.

ον, boneless, of the polypus, Hes. Op. 524 (Lacon. acc. to Clitarch. ap. Procl. ad loc.) cf. Hp. Epid. 2.2.19 ; ἀ. ἡ καρδία Arist. PA 666b17 ; τὰ περὶ τὴν κοιλίαν ib. 655a2 ; φυὴ μελέων Oppian. H. 1.639.

ον, unreturning, Orph. A. 1269.
whence none return, χῶρος ἐνέρων AP 7.467 (Antip.Sid.), cf. Oppian. H. 3.586, etc.

ον, not returning, κεῖνον ἀ. ἔθηκεν cut off his return, Od. 4.182.
not to be retraced, κέλευθος E. HF 431 (lyr.). (νόστος II) giving a low yield, of corn, Thphr. CP 3.21.1 (Sup.) ; not nutritious, Sor. 1.91.

ον, unreturning, without return, πάντας ὄλεσαν καὶ ἔθηκαν ἀνόστους Od. 24.528 ; πάντες ἐγένοντο ἄ. Arist. Fr. 145 ; Sup., ἡβάσεις ἥβαν ἀνοστοτάταν never, never to return, AP 7.482. = ἀνόστιμος ΙΙ, Thphr. CP 4.13.2 (Comp.).
ον, with no shell, ᾠά Sch. Nic. Al. 295.
ον, not stolen, Eust. 1768.54.
ον, that cannot be smelt, Arist. de An. 421b6.
ον, =ἀνόσφραντος, Alex.Aphr. de An. 52.15.
ἄνανδρος, Hsch.
ον, free from moisture, dry, τόποι Dsc. 1 Praef. 9 ; κονιορτός Archig. ap. Orib. 8.2.6.
ον, without the south wind, Hsch. s.v. βορεασμοί.
break out into wailing, A. Ag. 1074, E. Hel. 371 (lyr.).
ἀθρήνητον, Hsch. (ἀνότευκτον cod.).
ἄνω (Ion.), Hsch.
ον, without ear ; without handle, Theoc. Ep. 4.3.
ή, όν, of Anubis, epith. of a kind of thread, PMagPar. 1.1083.
άδος, ἡ, a plant, perh. = στάχυς, ib. 901.
τό, sanctuary of Anubis, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens 224 (Delos, ii BC).
τό, sanctuary of Anubis, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens 229, 231 (Delos, ii BC).

ον, unwarned, unadmonished, Isoc. 2.4, D. Ep. 3.11.
that will not be warned, Men. Mon. 49, Plu. 2.283f.
ἀνώλεθροι, Hsch.
ον, in Comp. -ότερον less wavy, cj. in Thphr. HP 3.11.3.
ἄβρεκτοι, ὑψηλοί, Hsch.
ουν, contr. for ἄνοος.

ον, = ἀνούσιος, opp οὐσιώδης, Corp.Herm. 2.5.
without the use of an οὐσία, PMagPar. 1.2441.

ον, without substance, οὐδὲ ἄρα ἡ ἑτερότης ἀ. Dam. Pr. 192 ; ἀ. καὶ νεκροί Procl. in Alc. p. 271C., cf. Olymp. in Alc. p. 92C. ; δύναμις, of God, opp. οὐσιώδης, Procl. Inst. 121. Adv. -ίως Syrian. in Metaph. 114.29. in Alchemy, not affecting substance, superficial in action, σώματα Zos.Alch. p 160B, al.
ητος, ἡ, unsubstantiality, Simp. in de An. 247.9.
εως, ἡ, conferring of non-existence, Simp. in Ph. 433.18.
ον, Ion. for ἄνοσος.

ον, unwounded bv stroke of sword, ἄβλητος καὶ ἀ. 11.4.540, cf. ARh. 2.75.
invulnerable, Nonn. D. 16.157, al.
where no wounds are inflicted, ἀγωνες ib. 37.774.

Adv without inflicting a wound, οὐδ’ ἄρα οἵ τις ἀνουτητί γε παρέστη Il. 22.371.
without receiving a wound, QS. 3.445.

ον, = ἀνούτατος, Nic. Th. 719.
invulnerable, Nonn. D. 16.382, etc.
prob. some kind of brushwood, PPetr. 3 p. 101.
ον, free from ophthalmia, Dsc. Eup. 1.29.
ον, without eyes, Tz. H. 3.219.
arch one΄s eyebrows ; metaph, to be supercilious, Com.Adesp. 842.
έως, ὁ, suspensory membrane, in pl., Aret. SA 2.6, 11.
ον, non-copulating, Arist. HA 546b16, al.
raise up, Olymp. in Mete. 24.13.

ἡ, holding back, stopping, esp. of hostilities ; hence mostly in pl., armistice, truce, X. Mem. 4.44.17 ; ἀνοχὰς ποιεῖσθαι Decr. ap. D. 18.164 ; διδόναι DH. 8.68 ; σπείσασθαι Plu. Pel. 29 ; αἱ Καλλισθένους ἀ. Aeschin. 2.31 ; αἱ ἑξαετεῖς ἀ. DH. 3.59 ; cf. ἀνοκωχή.
time, opportunity, οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἀνοχὴν ἐμβατεῦσαι LXX 1 Ma. 12.25 ; ἡμερῶν ἀ. delay of some days, POxy. 1068.15 (iii AD). pl., ἀνοχαί, = Lat. feriae, DC. 39.30. ἀνοχαὶ δικῶν, = Lat. iustitium, Id. 55.26.
(< ἀνέχομαι) long-suffering, forbearance, Ep. Rom. 2.4, 3.26. ἀνοχὴν ἀναπαύλης διδόναι permission to rest, Hdn. 3.6.10.
relief from disease, Philum. ap. Orib. Syn. 8.3.4. = ἀνατολή, Poll. 4.157, Hsch.
ἀνατολικός, Hsch. Adv. -κῶς connectedly, Simp. in de An. 285.19.
= ἀνοχλίζω, S.E. M. 10.83.
ἡ, = ἀοχλησία, Luc. Am. 27, DL. 2.87, Gal. 6.18.
ή, όν, heaving upwards. Adv. -κῶς S.E. M. 10.83.

heave up, ARh. 1.1167, Oppian. H. 5.128, Hsch.
heave out of the way, ARh. 3.1298.
ον, not in the way, not an impediment, Arist. PA 663b20 (Sup.).
hoist, lift up, AP 9.204 (Agath.).
τό, evacuation of the bowels, Thphr. HP 3.18.13.
ον, of weather, tolerable, Cat.Cod.Astr. 7.184.35.
fortify, dub. in Polyaen. 4.11.2.
ον, f.l. for ἀνώχυρος.
ἡ, want of fish (< ὄψον) to eat with bread, ἔφερον δεινῶς τὴν ἀ. Antiph. 190.8 ; ἀνοψίαν ὑποφέρειν Plu. 2.237f. Ion. ἀνοψίη, ἡ, = τὸ μὴ βλέπειν, Hsch. (ἀνοψοφίην cod.).
ον, (< ὄψον) without relish, Plu. 2.123b.
= ἐάνπερ, ἤνπερ, v. ἐάν.
= εἴθε, Sch. E. Or. 1580.
ἡ, coined by Pl. Cra. 413e as etym. of ἐνδρεία.
βουβών (Lacon.), Hsch.
ἅψασθαι, συνάψαι (Cret.), Hsch.
τὸ μόνον πρὸς τὸ πῦρ στῆυαι (Lacon.), Hsch.
poet. for ἀνασπάω.
poet. form, v. ἀνίστημι.
poet. form, v. ἀνίστημι.
poet. form, v. ἀνίστημι.
poet. form, v. ἀνίστημι.
poet. form, v. ἀνίστημι.
poet. form, v. ἀνίστημι.
poet. form, v. ἀνέχω.
poet. form, v. ἀνέχω.
v. ἀνασχετός.

Ep. Adv. over against, face to face, in Hom. mostly in the phrases, ἄ. μάχεσθαι fight man to man, Il. 19.163 ; ἄ. ἰδεῖν look before one, ib. 13.184, cf. E. Alc. 877 (lyr.) ; θεοῖς ἄ. ἐῴκει he was like the gods to look at, Il. 24.630 ; εἴδεται ἄ. πελιδνή Nic. Th. 238 ; ἄ. τιτύσκεσθαι aim straight at them, Od. 22.266, cf. Pi. N. 6.27 ; ἄ. πρός τινος Epigr.Gr. 223.4 (Milet.). as Prep. with gen., like ἀντί, over against, Ἤλιδος ἄ. Il. 2.626 ; ἄ. παρειάων σχομένη κρήδεμνα… before her cheeks, Od. 1.334 ; ἄντ’ ὀφθαλμοῖϊν 4.115 ; also of persons, ἄ. σέθεν before thee, to thy face, ib. 160, cf. 22.232 ; so in Il. 21.331, with a notion of comparison, confronted with thee ; ἕρπει ἄ. τῶ σιδάρω τὸ καλῶς κιθαρίσδεν rivals it, Alcm. 35. in hostile sense, against, Διὸς ἄ. πολεμίζειν Il. 8.428 ; Διὸς ἄ.… ἔγχος ἀεῖραι ib. 424 ; εἴ κέ μευ ἄ. στήης 17.29 ; Αἴαντος στήμεναι ἄ. ib. 166.
to be indignant in turn, Oenom. ap. Eus. PE 6.7.
love in turn or return, in Pass., Ph. 2.8, Them. Or. 4.55d.
rival as a collector, beggar, Celsus ap. Orig. Cels. 6.42.
shine brightly, Ps.-Callisth. 2.26.
buy with money received in payment for something else, πωλεῖν τι καὶ ἀ. σῖτον X. An. 1.5.5 ; τὰ ἀνταγορασθέντα D. 35.24.

speak against, reply, ἀνταγόρευσεν Pi. P. 4.156.
gainsay, contradict, τοῖς ἄρχουσιν Ar. Ra. 1072.
ἡ, adversity, dub. in IG 14.1977 (pl.).

struggle against, prove a match for, τινί, esp. in war, Hdt. 5.109, Th. 6.72, X. Cyr. 1.6.8, etc. ; ἀ. ταῖς παρασκεναῖς τινός D. 43.81 ; πρὸς τοὺς βαρβάρους Inscr.Prien. 17.15, cf. Ep. Hebr. 12.4. generally, struggle, vie with, τινί Th. 3.38 ; περί τινος And. 4.2 ; οἱ ἀνταγωνιζόμενοί τι the parties in a lawsuit, X. Cyr. 8.2.27 ; [οἱ ἐλευθέριοι] οὐκ ἀ. περὶ τῶν χρημάτων Arist. Rh. 1366b8.
act a part in rivalry with, τινί Plu. Dem. 29. as Pass., to be set against, τινί X. Oec. 10.12.
oppose, be a rival, Arist. Rh. 1416b14.

οῦ, ὁ, opponent, competitor, rival, Dialex. 2.7, X. Cyr. 1.6.8, 3.3.36, Alex. 272 ; τινί τινος X. Hier. 4.6, etc. ; ἀ. ἔρωτος a rival in love, E. Tr. 1006, cf. Pl. R. 554e, al. ; χαλεποὶ ἀ. τοῖς βαρβάροις Isoc. 4.75 ; ἀ. τῆς παιδείας opponents of their system of education, Arist. Pol. 1338b37 ; ἀ. ἔχειν τινὰ ταῖς ἐπιβολαῖς Plb. 2.45.5.
ον, in Poll. 3.141, is interpreted, contending as an adversary ; — but ἀνταγωνίστως (Id. 1.157) is f.l. for ἀναντ- in Lib. Decl. 15.21.
injure in return, retaliate upon, ἀλλήλους Pl. Tht. 173a, cf. Cri. 49b, 49c, Max.Tyr. 18.5.
one must retaliate, Max.Tyr. 18.5.

sing in answer, esp. of the partridge, answer when another calls, ἀ. ὡς μαχούμενος Arist. HA 614a11, cf. Mir. 845b25, Ael. NA 4.16 ; ἀ. Μούσαις Luc. Pisc. 6 ; τοῖς φθεγγομένοις Plu. 2.794c ; cry out at one, ἐγὼ δ΄, ἢν τοῦτο δρᾷς, ἀντᾴσομαι Ar. Ec. 887 ; — Pass., στροφῇ ἀντᾳσθῆναι Poll. 4.112.
= ἀνταίρω, only in Med., ἀνταείρεσθαι χεῖράς τινι raise one΄s hands against one, make war upon him, Hdt. 3.144, 7.101 ; or without τινί, 6.44.7.212 ; also πόλεμον βασιλέϊ ἀ. 8.140. a.
Dor. for ἀντήεις.
ον, contending against, rivalling, τινός AP 12.68 (Mel.).
ἄνεμοι, Hsch. (leg. ἀῆται).
Med., respect in return, αἰδουμένας ἀ. X. Cyr. 8.1.28.

α, ον, (< ἄντα) set over against, right opposite, ἀνταία πληγή a wound in front, right in the breast, S. El. 195, E. Andr. 844 ; ἀνταίαν ἔπαισεν (sc. πληγήν) S. Ant. 1308.
opposed to, hostile, hateful, κνώδαλον ἀ. βροτοῖσιν A. Ch. 588 (lyr.) ; πομπά E. IA 1323 (lyr.), cf. S. Fr. 72, 334 ; θεός ib. 335 ; τἀνταῖα θεῶν their hostile purposes, A. Pers. 604.
besought with prayers, epith. of Hecate, etc., ARh. 1.1141, cf. Orph. H. 41.1 ; ἀνταία·… ἱκέσιος, A. (Fr. 223) ap. Hsch. ; ἀνταῖος Ζεύς Sch. Il. 22.113.

Ion. ἀνταείρω, raise against, χεῖράς τινι AP 7.139 (so in Med., Th. 3.32, 1.53) ; πόλεμόν τινι Plb. 15.7.8 ; πρὸς Ἔρωτα μάχην AP 12.147 (Mel.) ; raise in reply, λαμπτῆρας Aen.Tact. 26.13 ; — Med., ὅπλα ἀνταιρόμενοι Th. 1.53, cf. 3.32.
intr., rise up or rebel against, withstand, ἀντᾶραί τινι Pl. Euthd. 272a, D. 2.24 ; πρός τι or τινα, Id. 6.5, Plu. Pyrrh. 15, DH. 6.48 ; — so in Med., τινί Luc. Herm. 33, JTr. 34. of a cliff, rise opposite to or in the same parallel with, τοῖς κατὰ Μερόην τόποις Str. 2.1.2, cf. 20 ; πρὸς τὴν Λιβύην Plu. Aem. 6.
to be ashamed in turn, Ach.Tat. 8.4.

demand in return, Th. 4.19, Lib. Or. 54.75 ; σμικρὰ τῆς ἀμνηστίας τὴν βουλήν App. BC 3.35.
contest with, τινὶ τὴν ὑπατείαν DC. 40.53.
make a countercharge, DC. Fr. 99.
rise over against, Plot. 6.5.11.
ὁ, a sort of sturgeon, Hdt. 4.53, Lync. 1.9, Ael. NA 14.23. Adj., τάριχος ἀν καῖον Antiph. 186.
σήμερον, and ἀντακές· σημεῖον (sic), Hsch. ; cf. ἀνταλλές.
v. sub ἀντακάς.

to be reciprocally implied, of the virtues, Chrysipp. Stoic. 3.72, cf. S.E. P. 1.68 (abs.) ; ἀ. ἀλλήλαις αἱ εὐφύειαι Anon. in Tht. 11.16 ; οὐδὲ ἀ. ἀλλήλαις [ἀκμὴ καὶ λαμπρότης] Hermog. Id. 1.10, cf. Them. in Ph. 150.29.
εως, ἡ, reciprocal implication, of the virtues, Stoic. 3.76, Procl. in Alc. p. 319C.
ἡ, = ἀντακολούθησις, Stoic. 2.121 ; correspondence, Iamb. in Nic. p. 39P.
ον, reciprocally implied, τὸ ἀ. ἀλλήλαις Eustr. in EN 311.15 ; abs., corresponding, ἕξις dub. in Phld. Rh. 1.27S. (cf. Supp. 15).
hurl against in return, λίθον DC. 59.28.

fut. -ούσομαι S. Aj. 1141, hear in turn, ἀντὶ τῶν εἰρημένων ἴσ’ ἀντάκουσον Id. OT 544 ; ἅ. γ’ εἶπας ἀντήκουσας E. Heracl. 1014 (cj.) ; κἀμοῦ νῦν ἀντάκουσον Id. Supp. 569 ; ἀντακούσει τοῦτον ὡς τεθάψεται S. Aj. 1141 ; abs., listen in return, ἀ. ἐν μέρει A. Eu. 198, cf. CratesCom. 5D. ; also in Prose, X. An. 2.5.16, Lib. Decl. 5.89.
hear in turn, Ar. Lys. 527.
τό, opposite headland, Str. 6.1.1.
boast in reply, Eust. 590.11.
return a shout, of friendly armies, Plu. Pyrrh. 32, Flam. 4 ; of an echo, A. Pers. 390.
ἡ, exchanging, exchange, barter, Gloss., Simp. in Ph. 1350.32.
ατος, τό, that which is given or taken in exchange, φίλου for a friend, E. Or. 1157, cf. LXX Jb. 28.15, al. ; τῆς ψυχῆς Ev. Matt. 16.26, cf. Ph. Fr. 110H.
ον, exchanged for another, Men. 16, 254, 513.
one must give in exchange, τινός for a thing, D. 19.223.
ου, ὁ, one who requites, τῶν κακῶν Phld. Mort. 17 (pl.).
ον, taken as equivalent, πρός τι Porph. Abst. 1.51.

Att. ἀνταλλάττω, exchange one thing with another, δάκρυα δ’ ἀνταλλάσσετε τοῖς τῆσδε μέλεσι E. Tr. 351 ; τὴν ἀξίωσιν τῶν ὀνομάτων ἐς τὰ ἔργα ἀ. they changed the signification of the names in relation to things, Th. 3.82 ; τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ χρυσίου Poll. 3.113. more freq. in Med., take in exchange, ἄνδρα A. Ch. 133 ; ἀνταλλάσσεσθαί τί τινος take one thing in exchange for another, E. Hel. 1088, etc. ; τι ἀντί τινος D. 16.5 ; ἀνταλλάσσεσθαι τῇ διανοίᾳ interchange in thought, Pl. Tht. 189c ; θάνατον ἀνταλλάξεται shall receive death in exchange, i.e. as a punishment, E. Ph. 1633 ; — so in Pass., ἀντηλλαγμένου τοῦ ἑκατέρων τρόπου having made an interchange of each other΄s custom, i.e. having each adopted the way of the other, Th. 4.14.
give in exchange, μηδεμιᾶς χάριτος μηδ’ ὠφελίας τὴν εἰς τοὺς Ἕλληνας εὔνοιαν D. 6.10.
ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας, Hsch. ; cf. ἀντακάς, ἀντακές.
ον, exchanged, Sch. DT. p. 343 H.

exchange one thing with another, ὅταν δελφῖσι θῆρες ἀνταμείψωνται νομόν Archil. 74.7. c. acc. pers., repay, requite, punish, ἀνταμείβεσθαί τινα κακοῖς Id. 65 ; κακαῖσι ποιναῖς A. Pr. 225 ; παθὼν κακῶς κακοῖσιν ἀντημείβετο Id. Th. 1054 ; ἀνταμειψόμεσθά σ’ ὥσπερ εἰκὸς ἀντὶ τῶνδε Ar. Th. 723.
answer again, τοῖσδε Hdt. 9.79 ; πρὸς τοὺς φίλους οἷ’ ἀνταμείβει ῥήματ’ S. OC 814 ; τινὰ οὐδέν ib. 1273 ; also ὑμᾶς… τοῖσδ’ ἀνταμείβομαι λόγοις E. Andr. 154.
εως, ἡ, exchanging, requital, v.l. in LXX Ps. 118 (119).112, Hsch.
in fut. Pass. ἀνταμεληθήσομαι, neglect in turn, Ph. 2.275.
ἀντερίζειν, Hsch.
sc. πούς, the foot ◡ ◡ – – ◡, Diom. 1.481 K.

ἡ, interchange, πυρὸς ἀ. τὰ πάντα καὶ πῦρ ἁπάντων Heraclit. 90.
repayment, requital, εὐεργεσίας Charito 5.2.
όν, v. ἀντημοιβός.

Med., defend oneself against another, resist, Th. 4.19.
requite, ἐχθρὸν κακοῖς S. Ant. 643 ; οἱ ἀνταμυνόμενοι Th. 3.84.
(< ἄμφοδον) miss a person in the street going to meet him, BGU 1030.5 (iii AD).
make go up in turn, X. HG 3.2.15.
cry out in answer or opposition, App. BC 2.131.
read and compare, Cratin. 386 ; νόμους D. 20 Arg. ii 8, cf. PPetr. 3 p. 50 (iii BC).

lead up against, esp. ἀ. νέας put ships to sea against, Hdt. 6.14, cf. Th. 7.37 ; also ἀ. ναυσὶν ἓξ καὶ ὀγδοήκοντα ib. 52 ; more freq. abs. in same sense, whether in Act., as Id. 8.38, X. HG 2.1.23, or in Med., as Th. 4.13, X. HG 1.1.5 ; — Pass., ναυσὶν ἀνταναχθείς DS. 13.71 ; — generally, attack, ἀντανήγετο πρὸς τὸ μειράκιον Pl. Erx. 398e.
raise in opposition, [ὄρος] τῇ Οἴτῃ Philostr. VA 4.23.
bring up instead, AP 9.285 (Phil.).

εως, ἡ, corresponding diminution, Arist. Top. 158b33.
alternate removal, Eust. 1397.44.
cancellation, Simp. in Ph. 1237.23.
α, ον, to be struck off, PTeb. 61 (6).220 (ii BC).
ή, όν, cancelling opposite sides of an account, striking a balance ; metaph, εὐλογιστία ἐστὶν ἐπιστήμη ἀνταναιρετική Stoic. 3.64.

strike out of an account, D. 18.231 ; — Pass., to be cancelled correspondingly, Arist. Metaph. 1040a22, Demad. 59 ; to be struck off, PTeb. 60.111, al. (ii BC).
kill in return, Ph. 2.321 (Pass.).
set off against, deduct, Sammelb. 4369 (a).10, al. (iii BC), PRyl. 154.33 (i AD, Pass.) ; prob. l. for ἀνταναίρειν (= ἀνθυφελεῖν), Ar. Fr. 12D.
Med., resume, ἀποβεβληκὼς τὴν ἁλουργίδα οὐκέτι ἀντανείλετο Agath. 4.29.

εως, ἡ, reflection of light, Placit. 4.14.3, cf. Vett.Val. 1.14, Ath.Med. ap. Orib. 9.12.1 (pl.) ; also, of sound, echo, Plu. 2.502d.
bending back, ἀγκίστρου Sch. Oppian. H. 1.216.
use of a word in an altered sense, Lat. contraria significatio, Quint. Inst. 9.3.68, Sch. ARh. 1.746.
ὁ, reflexive sense, of words, ADysc. Pron. 43.12.
ον, reciprocal, προσηγορία Priscian. Inst. 11.1.

reflect, φῶς v.l. in Plu. 2.696a ; — Pass., ἀντανακλᾶται ἀκτίς S.E. M. 5.82 ; ὀφθαλμοὶ ἀλλήλοις ἀντανακλώμενοι reflected one in another, Ach.Tat. 1.9. of sound, in Pass., to be reflected or echoed, LXX Wi. 17.19, Placit. 4.20.2.
bend back, τὸν ἀγκῶνα Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.13.8. Gramm., in Pass., to be reflexive, of pronouns, ADysc. Synt. 175.12, cf. Pron. 28.3, al.
cause to revert, in writing, εἴς τι πάλιν ἀ. τὸ πέρας CPHerm. 18.11.
ἡ, recoil, κυμάτων Arist. Mu. 396a19.
throw back again, Phryn. PS p. 61B.
cry out in turn or reply, App. Mith. 26.
take over instead, Ptol. Phas. p. 11H.
destroy in return, E. Or. 1165.
εως, ἡ, counteraction, incongruity of position, Vett.Val. 186.28, Antioch.Astr. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 8(3).107.
Astrol., counteract, Vett.Val. 289.17 (Pass.).
wait instead of taking active measures, c. inf., Th. 3.12.
Med., rest correspondingly, Polyaen. 1.14.
fill in return, v.l. in X. HG 2.4.12.
plait in rivalry with, ἄνθεα τοῖς Μελεαγρείοις στεφάνοις AP 4.2 (Phil.).

fill up, τὴν θέσιν τοῦ ὀνόματος ADysc. Synt. 14.1 ; τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ep. Col. 1.24 ; ἀ. πρὸς τὸν εὐπορώτατον ἀεὶ τοὺς ἀπορωτάτους put in the poorest so as to balance the richest, D. 14.17.
εως, ἡ, filling up again, Epicur. Ep. 1 p. 11U.
compensate, IG 14.956A 19.
return, of the foreskin, Paul.Aeg. 6.60.
bring back in turn, ἀ. τὴν πίστιν Plu. 2.20c. abs., make compensation, τῇ λοιπῇ δόξῃ πρὸς τὴν δυσφημίαν Them. Or. 7.99c.
give ground in turn, Aristid. Or. 23 (42).47.
ον, instead of a man, as a substitute, ἀντί τινος Luc. DMort. 16.2, etc.
(εἶμι ibo) rise so as to balance, τινί Th. 2.75.
ἡ, contrary wind, Simp. in de An. 60.32.
hold up in turn or in reply, πυρσούς Polyaen. 6.19.2, cf. 1.40.3, Men. Prot. p. 72D.
make equal adjust, compensate, Lib. Or. 59.161 (dub.) ; — Pass., Them. in Ph. 137.21.

set up against or in rivalry, λόγον Plu. 2.40e ; τρόπαιον DC. 42.48 ; τί τινι Plu. 2.348d. Pass., with aor.2 Act., rise up against, τινὶ ἐς χεῖρας S Tr. 441, cf. Plu. Sull. 7 ; rise one against another, Id. 2.723b.
ατος, τό, an equivalent, J. AJ 18.9.7.
εως, ἡ, balancing, equalizing, Boethus ap. Porph. ap. Eus. PE 11.28, David Proll. 214.11, Simp. in Cael. 458.2.
open against, ἀ. ὄμματα κεραυνοῖς face them, Longin. 34.4.
ἐπίβουλον, ἀντίδικον, Hsch.
v. ἀνατανύω.
ἐν μέρει, Hsch. (cf. ὑπαντάξ).

α, ον, also ος, ον Theoc. 17.114 : — worth just as much as, c. gen., ψυχῆς ἀ. worth life itself, Il. 9.401 ; πολλῶν ἀ. ἄλλων 11.514 ; ἕκαστος δέκα ἀνδρῶν ἀ. worth as much as ten, Hdt. 7.103, cf. 2.148, Pl. Lg. 730d, X. Mem. 2.10.3 etc. ; worthy of, τέχνας Theoc. l.c. abs., worth as much, worth no less, Il. 1.136.
demand as an equivalent or in turn, Th. 6.16 ; c. dupl. acc., ἀνταξιῶσαι δωρεὰν αὐτόν Macho ap. Ath. 13.570a.
demand in return, Th. 3.58, 5.17, Plu. Sol. 3 ; — Pass., to be called on for a thing in turn, λόγον Id. Cat. Mi. 53.
Med., obey in turn, ῥήτραις Tyrt. 4.6.
deceive in turn, τινά J. AJ 5.8.11.
threaten in turn, τινί Ph. 2.469, cf. Them. Or. 7.95b.
keep off in turn, AP 15.14 (Theoph.).
receive in return, χάριτάς τινος Anatolian Studies p. 343.

or ἀνταποδεικνύω, prove in return or answer, X. Smp. 2.22 ; τὸ ἀντικείμενον Arist. Rh. 1403a27.
appoint instead, DC. 49.43.
= ἀνταποδείκνυμι.

give back, repay, tender in repayment or requital, Batr. 186 ; ἀ. τὸ ὅμοιον, τὸ ἴσον, Hdt. 1.18, Th. 1.43 ; χάριν Pherecr. 2D. ; τὴν ἴσην Arist. Rh. 1379b7 ; ἀ. τροφεῖα Lys. 6.49 ; ἀρετήν Th. 4.19 ; ὕβριν Plu. 2.825c ; τὰ αὐτὰ ἀ. react in the same way, Pl. Ti. 79e ; of counter-arguments, Id. Prm. 128d ; abs., pay back, Th. 3.40, Arist. Rh. 1367a21.
take vengeance, LXX De. 32.35, al., Ep. Rom. 12.19.
assign as a balance, ἐναντίαν γένεσιν Pl. Phd. 71e.
make convertible, τὴν μεταφορὰν τὴν ἐκ τοῦ ἀνάλογον Arist. Rh. 1407a15 ; — Pass., Demetr. Eloc. 79. Gramm., make to correspond, of correlatives (e.g. τοιοῦτος, οἷος), in Pass., ADysc. Conj. 254.19, Synt. 54.5, al. ; so of μέν… δέ, Arist. Rh. 1407a23, Demetr. Eloc. 53, cf. Hermog. Id. 1.4, al.
intr., answer to, correspond with, εἰ μὴ ἀνταποδιδοίη τὰ ἕτερα τοῖς ἑτέροις Pl. Phd. 72a, cf. b ; οὐκ ἀνταποδίδωσι τὸ ὅμοιον there is no similar correspondent, Arist. Mete. 347b32, cf. IA 707b16, Ps.-Alex.Aphr. in SE 192.14.
give back words, exchange ΄tu quoque΄s΄, Pl Phdr. 236c.
deliver in turn, τὸ σύνθημα X. Cyr. 3.3.58 (Pass.) ; explain in turn, Pl. Ti. 87c.
give back a sound, of an echo, Plu. Sull. 19 ; of troops, κραυγὴν ἀ. Id. Tim. 27.
ατος, τό, repayment, requital, whether of good or evil, LXX Si. 12.2, 14.6, al., Ev. Luc. 14.12, Ep. Rom. 11.9.

εως, ἡ, giving back in turn, opp. ἀποδοχή, Th. 4.81 ; rendering, requiting, repayment, Arist. EN 1133a3, 1163a11, al. ; χάριτος Men. Mon. 330, DS. 20.100 ; τῶν εὐεργεσιῶν Phld. Piet. 14 ; retribution, LXX Is. 61.2, 63.4, al. ; reprisals, γίγνεται ἀ. ἔκ τινος Plb. 5.30.6 ; reward, LXX Ps. 18 (19).11, Ep. Col. 3.24.
turning back, opposite direction or course, of a current, ἀ. ποιεῖσθαι Plb. 4.43.5, etc., cf. Plu. 2.136b.
responsive sound, Arist. Aud. 803a31.
alternation, e.g. of action and reaction, περιόδων πρὸς ἀλλήλας Hp. Aph. 1.12 ; reaction, prob. in Epicur. Ep. 2 p. 48U., cf. Thphr. Vent. 10. Rhet., parallelism or opposition of clauses in a periodic sentence, Demetr. Eloc. 23, cf. 250 ; in a simile, correspondence with the object of comparison, Quint. Inst. 8.3.77. Gramm., correlativity of words such as τοιοῦτος, οἷος, ADysc. Synt. 54.1.
answering clause, Hermog. Id. 1.11, 2.1 ; v l. in ADysc. Synt. 20.6.
capping verses, as a subject of competition, Michel 913 (Teos).
one must repay, τὴν ἀξίαν ὧν ἔπαθεν Arist. EN 1163a2 ; τιμήν 1163b14 ; χάριν 1164b26 ; τὰς εὐεργεσίας ib. 31. ἀ. ἕξιν τινί one must make it correspond to…, Pl. Phlb. 40d.

ή, όν, = ἀμοιβαῖος, Sch. Oppian. H. 2.255.
Gramm., belonging to or marking ἀνταπόδοσις, Plb. Rh. p. 107S. ; of pronouns, correlative, ADysc. Adv. 158.24, Conj. 237.9, al. Adv. -κῶς Sch. ARh. 1.5.
strip, prepare for a contest with, τινί Philostr. Im. 2.19.
die or am killed in requital, ἀνταποθανεῖν τὸν ἀποκτείναντα Antipho 5.10 ; τοῦ ἐμψύχου δόγματος ὃ ἀνεῖλε Ph. 1.94.
f.l. for ἀντίποινα, S. Ph. 316, E. HF 755 ; also in POxy. 1381.234.

εως, ἡ, renewal by substitution, Corp.Herm. 11.2.
of planets, the opposite position to ἀποκατάστασις, Doroth. ap. Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.196.19.
ή, όν, Astrol., opposite to the position of ἀποκατάστασις, σελήνη Max. Epit. p. 80 L.

Med., answer again, LXX Jb. 16.8, Ev. Luc. 14.6 ; argue against, τινί Ep. Rom. 9.20.
IΙ. correspond to, Nicom. Ar. 1.8.10, 11.
εως, ἡ, correspondence (cf. ἀνταποκρίνομαι II), ib. 8, Iamb. in Nic. p. 36P.
kill in return, Hdt. 7.136, A. Ch. 121, E. Hec. 262, Ar. Ach. 326, X. HG 2.4.27, etc.
receive or accept in return, ἑστίασιν Pl. Ti. 27b ; χάριν D. 20.46.
destroy in return, E. Ion 1328, Pl. Cri. 51a. Pass. and Med., with pf. 2 Act., perish in turn, αὐτὸς ἀνταπωλόμην E. Hel. 106, cf. IT 715 ; ὑπὲρ ἀνδρὸς ἑκάστου δέκα ἀνταπόλλυσθαι Hdt. 3.14.
speak for the defence or in reply, Is. 5.17, DC. 50.2.
lose what one has won at play, ἀστραγάλους Menecr. 1D.
εως, ἡ, rebounding, revulsion, Cass. Pr. 26.
Lat. oppedere, πρὸς τὰς βροντάς Ar. Nu. 293.
raise questions in turn, S.E. M. 1.231.

send in exchange, ὁμήρους Plb. 21.43.22 ; send backwards and forwards, πρέσβεις DC. 50.2, cf. Aen.Tact. 31.9 (Pass.) ; refer one back again, ἐπί τι S.E. M. 8.86 ; of an echo, τὰς ἀνακλάσεις ἀ. Plu. 2.248c.
turn back again, Tz. H. 5.903.
ἡ, turning away from one another, of places which face opposite ways, Str. 6.1.5.
cut off in turn by trenches, App. BC 2.61.
wall off, fortify on the other side, DC. 43.7.
requite, repay, AP 9.223 (Bianor), Orph. Fr. 32d, e.
συνδεδεμένος, Hsch.
show on the other hand, Th. 3.38, 67.
catch in turn, of a ball, Poll. 9.107.
τό, counter-receipt, POxy. 1542.1 (iv AD), BGU 974.10 (iv AD).
Ion. for ἀνθάπτομαι.
repel in turn, Arist. Pr. 936b35 ; — Pass., Id. Somn. Vig 457b23.
εως, ἡ, mutual repulsion, Placit. 2.23.2.
ἀετός (Etruscan), Hsch. = δίασμα, Euph. 147.
Dor. for ἀντήρης.
ου, ὁ, the star a Scorpii, Heph.Astr. 1.3, Ptol. Calend. p. 214W., Id. Alm. 8.1.
count against one another, Paus. 10.20.1.
ἑκάστῳ σταγόνι τοὺς ἴσους [ὀδόντας] Poll. 2.93.
hold out against, τοῖς παροῦσιν Th. 7.15 ; πρός τι Plu. Cleom. 30. abs., hold out, persist, Ar. Eq. 540, Isoc. 6.79, 19.26 ; c. part., τρέφουσα… ἀντήρκεσεν DC. 68.25.
ή, όν, antarctic, πόλος Arist. Mu. 392a4 ; κύκλος Gem. 5.16 ; without κύκλος, ib. 39 ; ζώνη Placit. 3.14.1.
ἡ, insurrection, Lyd. Ost. 33, Cat.Cod.Astr. 7.171.
εως, ἡ, = ἀνταρσία, Sm. 4Ki. 11.14.
τύραννος, ἐπιβαίνων βασιλεῖ, Hsch.
ὁ, pro-magistrate, Gloss.
οντος, ὁ, vice-president, τοῦ ἀγῶνος IG2². 1077, cf. ib. 12(2).35e (Mytil.) ; pro-magistrate, SIG 785.17 (Chios), POxy. 907.21 (iii AD) ; ἀ. τῶν στρατηγῶν AJA 18.329 (Sardes, i BC).
πνοάς, Hsch. (leg. ἀήτας).
welcome, greet in turn, X. Cyr. 1.3.3 ; return greeting, Hierocl. Facet. 7 ; receive kindly, X. Cyr. 5.55.42, Pl.Com. 12D., Plu. Tim. 38.
lighten against, ἀστραπαῖς DC. 59.28.
α, ὁ, (< ἄτη) surety, GDI 5015.23 (Gortyn).
requite with dishonour, prob. cj. in S. Aj. 1339.

= ἀνταυγέω, πρὸς ἥλιον Hld. 1.2, cf. 9.14.
trans., expose to the light, illuminate, ἡλίῳ βίον ἀ. Ph. 2.260.
ἡ, reflection of light, Gloss..

or ἀνταυγία, ἡ, reflection of light, Placit. 2.20.12, X. Cyn. 5.18, Plu. 2.921b, Ps.-Hp. Hebd. 1.52 ; ἡλίου Onos. 29.2 ; τῆς χιόνος from the snow, DS. 17.82 ; shining in one΄s face, ἡλίου Ascl.Tact. 12.10.
reflect light, Hp. Carn. 17, Arist. Pr. 932a27, Chaerem. 14 ; πρὸς Ὄλυμπον Emp. 44 ; φάσγανον ἀνταυγεῖ φόνον flashes back murder, E. Or. 1519 ; gleam, glitter, Eub. 56.
ές, reflecting light, sparkling, κάλλος Sannyr. 1D. ; κόραι Ar. Th. 902 ; χιών DS. 17.82 ; pr. n. Ἀνταύγης, of the sun, Orph. Fr. 237.
= ἀνταύγεια.
address face to face, τινά S. El. 1478.
play on the flute against, τινί Agath. 4.23.
sound in turn, answer, οἱ ἀντάϋσε [υ] βροντᾶς φθέγμα Pi. P. 4.197, cf. Opp. C. 2.78.
εως, ἡ, subtraction from the opposite side, Nicom. Ar. 1.13.

take away in return, in Med., Antipho 4.1.7 ; — Act., intr., diminish in turn, Aristid. Or. 23 (42).50, cf. 2.309J.
subtract from the opposite side, and ἀνταφαίρεσις, εως, ἡ, subtraction from the opposite side, Nicom. Ar. 1.13.
feast in return, Pl. Ti. 17b.

let go in turn, δάκρυ ἀ. let the tear fall in turn, E. IA 478.
send back, σφαῖραν Poll. 9.107.
Dor. for ἀντηχέω.

Ep. impf. ἤντεον Il. 7.423 ; c. dat. pers., come opposite to, meet face to face, meet with, ἥ οἱ ἔπειτ’ ἤντησ’ ib. 6.399 ; ἤντεον ἀλλήλοισιν 7.423 ; so also in Trag., ἀνέμοις ἀ. A. Supp. 36 ; πατρί S. Tr. 902, etc. = ἀντιάω, c. gen., c. gen. pers., meet in battle, εἴ κεν πάντων ἀντήσομεν Od. 16.254, cf. Il. 16.423 ; also without any hostile sense, σπέρμα μὲν ἄντασ’ Ἐρεχθειδᾶν by lineage she reached, went up to the Erechtheidae, S. Ant. 982. c. gen. rei, meet with, take part in, partake in or of, μάχης, δαίτης, Il. 7.158, Od. 3.44 ; κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς how thou hast gained sight of him, ib. 17.44, cf. 3.97 ; so ἀ. ξεινίων Hdt. 2.119 ; ἁλώσιος Pi. O. 10 (11).42 ; ἀ. τινὸς ὑπό τινος meet with such and such treatment from another, Hdt. 1.114 ; σφῷν… θεοῖς ἀρῶμαι μή ποτ’ ἀντῆσαι κακῶν S. OC 1445. c. acc., ἤν νιν πομπαῖς ἀντήσῃς E. IA 150 (s.v.l.). — The simple Verb never in Com. or Att. Prose ; but cf. ἀπαντάω.
insert one name instead of another, Arist. Ath. 36.2, D. 25.73 (Pass.).
raise or build instead, DC. 69.12 ; build in opposition, τί τινι App. Pun. 114.

make a counter-claim, D. 40.14.
bring a countercharge, τινί Isoc. 17.12, DH. 8.64, Plu. Ant. 55, etc. ; ἀλλήλοις δώρων Hermog. Stat. 3.

Pass., to be urgent on the other side, Eun. VS p. 470B.
to be inserted in place of another letter (as θ for ε), Eust. 1863.56.
ατος, τό, counter-claim or -charge, Hermog. Stat. 2, cf. 11 ; pl., Corn. Rh. p. 387H.
ή, όν, of or for a counter-accusation, ἀντίθεσις Hermog. Stat. 6, 12 ; τὸ ἀντεγκληματικόν Antipho 4.2 Arg. ; τὰ ἀντεγκληματικά Aps. p. 235H. Adv. -κῶς Sch. ARh. 1.834.
entrust to another instead, τινὶ δίκας DC. 60.24.
pour in instead, Gal. 18(1).282.
fut. -άσομαι Pl. Men. 80c ; aor. -ῄκασα Ar. V. 1311, subj. -εικάσω Pl. l.c. : — compare in return, τινά τινι Ar. l.c. ; c. acc., Pl. l.c. ; — hence ἀντεικασία, ἡ, Sch. Ven. Il. 8.560.
v. ἀντεικάζω.
unwind in opposite direction, Orib. 49.22.18 (Pass.).
ὁ ἐναντίος τῇ ἀγωγῇ, Hsch.
poet. for ἀνατείνω.

aor.2 without any pres. (cf. ἀντερῶ, ἀντιλέγω, ἀνταγορεύω), speak against or in answer, gainsay, c. dat., S. OC 999, etc. ; ἀ. τινὶ δεομένῳ Th. 1.136 ; abs., οὐδὲν ἀντειπεῖν ἔχω A. Pr. 51 ; ἀ. πρός τινα or τι, Th. 3.61, X. HG 3.3.3 ; oppose, Pl. Thg. 131a ; ἀ. ὑπέρ τινος speak in one΄s defence, Ar. Th. 545 ; c. acc. cogn., ἀ. ἔπος utter a word of contradiction, E. IA 1391 ; δύο λόγω περὶ τῶν αὐτῶν ἀντειπεῖν speak on both sides of a question, Isoc. 10.1 ; τούτῳ ἂν δίκαιον λόγον ἀντείποιμι Pl. Ap. 28b. κακῶς ἀ. τινά malign him in turn, S. Ant. 1053.
Ion. aor. -ειρόμην, Att. -ηρόμην : — ask in turn, Hdt. 1.129, 3.23, X. Cyr. 2.2.22 ; in part., Plu. 2.739b.

introduce, import instead, D. 9.39 (Pass.), Pl. Ax. 369e, Men. 402.16, etc.
bring in to office, etc., in turn, ἀλλήλους εἰς ἐπαρχίας κτλ. Plu. Caes. 14.
restore, Gal. 6.75, al.
ἡ, compensatory antithesis (as οἰκτρόν… σεμνὸν δέ), Alex. Fig. 1.25, Zonae. Fig. 20.
v.l. for ἀντεισενεκτέον one must restore, Gal. 1.393.
intr., make an inroad in reprisal, DC. 48.21.
enter instead, εἰς τοὺς πόρους Eust. 1111.45.
(εἶμι ibo) enter in turn or in return, Simp. in Ph. 573.4.
one must introduce instead, Hermog. Stat. 3.
enter in turn or instead, Aristid. Or. 37 (2).27, Hero Spir. 2.36, Them. in Ph. 113.26.
to be introduced in place of, Hero Spir. 1.3.
bring in, introduce in turn, Sch. DT. p. 72H.

contribute in return, τὰς εἰσφοράς Ar. Lys. 654 ; metaph, οὐδὲ τυχόντα ἔρανον ἀλλήλαις Gal. UP 8.7. νόμον ἀ. substitute a new law for an old one, D. 20.97 ; καινὰ δαιμόνια DC. 52.36.
introduce as a countor measure, Onos. 42.12.
ἡ, contribution in return, Milet. 3 No.147.22 (iii BC).
to be produced in an opposite direction, Theol.Ar. 26 ; ἀλλήλοις to be correspondingly projected, Anon. in EN 224.24.
ὁ, deputy defensor, POxy. 1987 (vi AD, cf. PLond. 5.1709.80 (vi AD).
rush out on the other side from, Arr. An. 1.21.3.
squeeze out in turn, Hp. Loc. Hom. 9.
kindle in turn, metaph of passion, J. AJ 15.7.3 (Pass).
steal away in return, Ar. Ach. 527.
carry out or away in return, in fut. ἀντεκκομιεῖ, Hsch.
knock out in return, ὀφθαλμόν D 24.140 ; εἴ τις τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν ἐξέκοψέ τινος, ἀντεκκοπῆναι Arist. MM 1194a38, cf. DS. 12.17.
excrete in turn, Gal. 4.517 (Pass.).
send out in turn, X. HG 4.8.25 ; expel, discharge in turn, of respiration, Gal. 5.710.
sail out against, τινί Th. 4.13 ; abs., Plu. Lys. 10.
frighten in return, Ael. NA 12.15, Aristid. 1.130J.
breathe out in turn, Gal. Nat. Fac. 3.13, al.
flow out in turn, ib. 1.13, UP 6.11.
ἀνταπόδοσις, Hsch.
(sc. στρατόν), draw up troops in opposition, App. BC 4.108.
stretch out in rivalry, ἀ. αὑτόν τινι match oneself with another, Ar. Ra. 1042 ; τῇ ἐκείνου δεινότητι τὸν ἐκείνου πλοῦτον Philostr. VS 1.21.4.

set forth or state instead, Plu. Arat. 1 ; publish a counter-edict, Id. CG 12.
contrast with, S.E. M. 1.251.
repay, Ph. 2.78, al.
εως, ἡ, retribution, Ph. 1.159 ; requital, Sch. Pi. P. 1.112.
ον, (< ἐκτίνω) punished in turn, Sch. Il. 24.213. [To be deleted (Suppl.)]

to maintain in return ; — in Pass., ἀντεκτρέφεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκγόνων Arist. HA 615b25.
train as a rival, βότρυν βότρυϊ Lync. ap. Ath. 14.654a.
sally out against, X. HG 4.3.17, Ages. 2.10.
bring out against, oppose, τί τινι Plu. 2.72e.
grow out, issue opposite, Gal. 5.537.
to be worsted in turn, DC. 44.27.
intr., sail against, τριήρει with a trireme, Plu. Nic. 24.
ὁ, Ion. for ἀνθελ-.
deduct, POxy. 1578.11 (iii AD).
ὁ, compensation, Gloss.
ὁ, = ἀντελλογισμός ; metaph, ἐν ἀντελλόγῳ σταθμᾶσθαι Eust. 997.54.
poet. for ἀνατέλλω.
hope instead or in turn, ἄλλα Th. 1.70 ; ἕτερον πλοῦτον Lib. Decl. 26.28.
fit into each other, of hinge-joints (< γίγγλυμοι), Gal. 2.737 ; — also ἀντέμβασις, εως, ἡ, ibid.

put in instead, τῇ γῇ παγκαρπίαν Thphr. HP 9.8.7 ; substitute, Dsc. 2.49.
intr., make an inroad in turn, X. HG 3.5.4, Plb. 5.96.3 ; attack in turn, Plu. Phil. 18.
v. sub ἀντεμβαίνω.
put on board instead, Th. 7.13, cf. D. 4.37.
shout at a person in answer, AB 85, Eust. 855.21.
ἡ, answering cry, Anon. in Rh. 3.580W.

ἡ, pipe made of pieces fitted into each other, BGU 1117.16 (13 BC), cf. 1116.12. = ἀντέμβασις, Hsch. s.v. ἐπαλλάξαντες, Suid. s.v. γίγγλυμοι.
substitute, κίκεως PHolm. 10.11.
ἀντεξετάζειν, Hsch.
ἡ, remedy for external application, Orib. Fr. 90.
requite an injury, dub. word in E. Fr. 611 (= Eup. 458).
mock at in return, τινί Sch. Ar. Pax 1112.
in Pass., resist and become fixed, of barbs, Paul.Aeg. 6.88.
aor.2 -ενεπάγην, Pass., to be plunged in in revenge, τισί Ar. Ach. 230.
fill in turn, ἀντενέπλησαν τὴν ὁδόν X. HG 2.4.12 ; fill in return, by way of compensation, τί τινος Id. An. 4.5.28 ; — Pass., to be filled with in exchange, τινός Pl. Lg. 705b.
set on fire in return, ἀντενεπίμπρασαν τὰ ἱρά Hdt. 5.102.
fall into the place of, Phlp. in Ph. 547.19 ; attack in return, Agath. 5.19.
Pass., to be entwined together, ἀλλήλαις Dsc. 4.75, cf. Poll. 1.184 ; of crossed or reversed bandaging, Sor. Fasc. 12.513C. : — return one΄s embraces or salutation, J. AJ 16.2.5.
ἡ, mutual entwining, αἱ ἐν ταῖς ἀτόμοις ἀ. M.Ant 7.50 ; crossing of veins, Gal. in Pl. Ti. 7 ; complication, confusion, M.Ant 6.10.
oppose by a counter-statement, ἀ. ταῖς ἀποφάσεσιν Plb. 18.28.12.
= ἀντεμφαίνω, Hsch.
εως, ἡ, difference of appearance, Str. 2.4.8 ; also pl., ibid. ; opposition, antithesis, S.E. M. 1.57 ; distinction, Hdn. Gr. 1.941, ADysc. Adv. 159.19.
obstruct, Simp. in Cael. 441.7.
to be inserted opposite, Gal. 4.384.
εως, ἡ, Rhet., positive statement made in a negative form, as οὐκ ἐλάχιστα for μέγιστα, Alex. Fig. 2.23, Zonae. Fig. 22.
give contrary indications, of symptoms, Gal. 10.626.
εως, ἡ, counter-indication, Steph. in Hp. 2.282D.
give way in turn, of sawyers, ὁ μὲν ἕλκει, ὁ δ’ ἀντενέδωκε Ar. V. 694 (Dobree, for ἀντανέδωκε).
put on instead, Plu. 2.139c.
ἡ, counter-ambuscade, Plb. 1.57.3.
lay a counter-ambuscade, Hp. Ep. 17, DC. 41.51.
to be efficacious against, θανασίμοις Dsc. 1.115.
take a counter-pledge, Hsch. s.v. ῥυσιάζει.
τό, counter-pledge, Sch. ARh. 1.1355.
εως, ἡ, insertion instead, Eust. 1079.12.
insert instead, prob. rest. in IGRom. 4.293 i37 (Pergam., ii BC, Pass.).
introduce as inhabitants instead ; — Pass., αἱ ψυχαί ἁγνοῖς πάλιν ἀ. σώμασιν J BJ 3.8.5.
insert in turn or instead, Nicom. Ar. 2.27.

export in return, X. Vect. 3.2.
evict in return, BGU 1273.34 (iii BC ; written ἀντιεξ-).
lead out against, τὰ στρατόπεδα Plb. 2.18.6, cf. DH. 8.65, Plu. Publ. 9 ; v.l. for προσήγαγε, DS. 13.66 ; — abs., march out against, τινί Plb. 3.66.11.
raise to an equal height, λόγοις ἔργα Philostr. VS 1.19.1.
demand in return, Plu. Alex. 11.
Pass., with aor.2 Act., rise up against, πρός τι Hld. 7.19.
deceive in return, DC. 58.18.
ατος, τό, (< ἀντεξαίρω) southerly elevation (i.e. latitude), corresponding to a northerly one, Theol.Ar. 25.
(εἶμι ibo) go out against, X. HG 4.5.10, Plb. 1.24.10.
charge against, attack, Plu. Phil. 18, al., DC. 47.43.
= ἀντέξειμι, X. HG 7.2.12, Cyr. 6.3.13.

try one by the standard of another, Aeschin. 1.8, 37, Arr. Epict. 2.18.21 ; τι πρός τι Plu. Caes. 3, cf. Gal. 18(1).229 ; τινὰ ἀλλήλοις Them. in Ph. 52.20 ; compare, λόγους Luc. Herm. 30, cf. Aps. p. 247 H., etc. ; — Pass., to be measured or compared, παρά or πρός τι, Plu. Tim. 36, 2.65b ; τινί Ph. 2.45, al., D.Chr. 31.126 ; — Med., measure one΄s strength against another, τινί Luc. DMort. 12.2 ; esp. dispute with him at law, like ἀντιδικέω, ib. 29.1 ; metaph, ἀ. τῇ νόσῳ Id. Abd. 16.

εως, ἡ, comparison, ADysc. Synt. 161.10, Aps. p. 248H., al.
term of comparison, of an integer compared with the sum of the preceding integers, Theol.Ar. 10.
one must compare, Max.Tyr. 30.6.
ή, όν, comparative, Aphth. Prog. 10. Adv. -κῶς Men. Rh. p. 403S.
εως, ἡ, counter-explanation, αἱ πρὸς Ἰόβαν ἀ., title of work by Didymus, Ath. 14.634c.
οῦ, ὁ, deputy-ἐξηγητής BGU 362 xv 10 (iii AD), PMeyer 6.9 (ii AD), PRyl. 397.1 (iii AD).
ride out against, Plu. Pomp. 7.
make equal, compare, Sch. Od. 11.308.
Pass., with aor.2 Act., yield to an altack, retire from the contest, Plu. 2.946d.
ἡ, a military movement, τὰς δι’ ἀλλήλων ἀ. καὶ εἰσόδους Onos. 10.2.
sail or march out against, DC. 48.47, 63.24.
εως, ἡ, sailing against, v.l. in Th. 2.91 ; countercharge, Plu. Pomp. 69.
εως, ἡ, counter-thrust, Epicur. Ep. 2 p. 40U.

lead against ; abs. (sc. στρατόν or the like), advance against, advance to meet an enemy, Th. 4.124, Plb. 12.18.11, etc.
inflict in return, ποινήν τινι Aristaenet. 2.9.
introduce as a counter-measure, ἀλεξήματα Onos. 30.
use charms against, Plot. 4.4.43.
praise in return, X. Cyr. 8.3.49. Pass., ἀ. τινι to be extolled in comparison with, Luc. Pr. Im. 19.
one must march against, πρός τινα Onos. 21.6.
put to sea against, πρός τινα Th. 4.25.
ὁ, subpraefectus, Gloss.
let go, let slip against, τινί Luc. Zeux. 9.
(εἶμι ibo) rush upon, meet an advancing enemy, Th. 4.33, 96, etc. ; τινί Id. 7.6, cf. Lib. Decl. 37.15, Onos. 8.2 ; πρός τι Id. 21.8.
to be carried in or enter instead, Ti.Locr. 102a ; f.l. for ἀντεπείσειμι, Placit. 4.22.1.
(εἶμι ibo) enter in turn, εἰς τὰ ἀραιώματα ibid.
ἡ, entrance in return, ἀ. παρέχειν ibid.
come in instead, ib. 2.
εως, ἡ, stretching in the opposite direction, Hsch. s.v. τόξου πῆχυν.
stretch in the contrary direction, Gal. 18(1).213.
rush to meet, attack one, App. Pun. 26.
intr., sail or march out against, Th. 8.104, Luc. Bacch. 3 ; c. acc., στρατιάν, δύναμιν, J. AJ 6.9.1, 8.14.4 ; — also in Med., DC. 50.31.
(εἶμι ibo) march out to meet an enemy, πρός τινα Th. 7.37 ; abs., X. Cyr. 3.3.30, etc.
= ἀντεπέξειμι, Th. 4.72.
= ἀντεπέξειμι, ib. 131, Aristid. 1.149J.
ἡ, sally in turn, DC. 47.37.
obnitor, Gloss.
march against in return, Aristid. 1.150J., cf. DC. 36.51.
restipulor, Gloss. ask a question in turn, PLond. 1.118(1).70 (vi AD).
εως, ἡ, restipulatio, Gloss.
clamour against one, Luc. Cat. 19.
form counter-designs, Th. 1.33, 3.12, etc.
write something instead, καλὰ ἐπιγράμματα ἀνελὼν ἀσεβῆ ἀ. D. 22.72 ; — Med., ἀντεπιγράφεσθαι ἐπὶ τὸ νίκημα put their own names instead of the other party to the victory, i.e. claim it, Plb. 18.34.2.

exhibit in turn, Pl. Tht. 162b ; c. part., contrast, ἀ. ἑαυτὸν ποιοῦντά τι X. Ages. 1.12 ; — Med., exhibit oneself in competition, Plu. 2.674b ; also c. acc. rei, ἀ. τι καλόν τινι display a fine sight in rivalry with, Id. Ant. 23 ; also τι πρός τι Id. Alex. 21.
εως, ἡ, mutual attack, contention, Ph. 1.7, al.
desire a thing in rivalry with, τινός And. 4.28 ; — Pass., ἐπιθυμῶν ξυνεῖναι καὶ ἀντεπιθυμεῖσθαι τῆς ξυνουσίας and have one΄s company desired in turn, X. Mem. 2.6.28.
offer sacrifice as substitute, BCH 15.207.
accuse in return, ἀ. ὅτι… App. BC 5.59.
to be placed upon, Gal. 12.604.
put a price on one΄s head in return, χρήματά τινι Poll. 4.93.
help in return, τινί X. HG 4.6.3.
ἡ, alternate mastery, νείκους καὶ φιλίας Placit. 2.4.8.
get the upper hand in turn, Str. 16.1.19, DC. 44.27.
lay hold on the other side, Luc. Symp. 43.
or ἀντεπιμέλομαι, attend or give heed in turn, v.l. X. Cyr. 5.1.18 ; τινός to one, Id. An. 3.1.16.
v.l. for ἀντιμέλλω.
= ἀντεπιμελέομαι.
measure to in return, Poll. 5.142.
devise in turn, Ael. NA 6.23, J. AJ 10.8.1 ; c. inf., App. BC 4.109.
sail against in turn, Th. 1.54 and prob. in 1.50, Poll. 1.124.
admit a counter-fluxion, Hp. Loc. Hom. 29.
ατος, τό, counter-ἐπίρρημα, Heph. Poëm. 8.2, Poll. 4.112 ; v. ἐπίρρημα.
mock in return, τινά Plb. 18.7.5.
gloss on ἀνθέλκω, Hsch. ; — Med., Ph. 1.247 ; absorb nutriment, Gal. 17 (2).312.
ατος, τό, return furnished in reply, CPR 20i20 (iii AD).
ή, όν, of or for replying to a letter ; ἀντεπισταλτική (sc. τέχνη), ἡ, art of writing replies, Epist.Charact. 19.
ου, ὁ, vice-president, τοῦ Μουσείου, Recueil de Travaux 37.94 (Denderah).
write an answer, CPR 20ii5 (iii AD) ; c. inf., J. AJ 15.6.2, al. ; οὐδέν Luc. Sat. 19 ; — Pass., τὰ ἀντεπεσταλμένα Paus. 4.22.6, etc.
take the field against, X. HG 4.8.33.
turnagainst, retort, Plu. 2.810e ; turn round and back, of a needle, Gal. 10.418.
ἡ, turning back upon, χειρὸς ἐπὶ τὸν ὦμον Placit. 4.14.3 ; κατ’ ἀ. Ruf. ap. Orib. 49.35.4.
order in turn, τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Th. 1.135 ; τινί τι Pl. Ti. 20b.
excite by contrast, τὴν φαντασίαν Plu. 2.933c.
raise a counter-work ; metaph, Λυκείῳ τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἀ. Him. Or. 7.13 ; so as Dep. with pf. Pass., establish a fort in the enemy΄s country, Th. 1.142.

put on in exchange, DC. 58.7 (Pass.). ἀ. ἐπιστολὴν πρός τινα give a letter in answer, Th. 1.129, Is. Fr. 49, cf. J. AJ 17.5.1.
Med., make a counter-attack, throw oneself upon, DS. 36.4, Ph. 1.661 ; simply, attack, 2.111 ; — Act. in same sense, ἀλλήλοισιν make mutual plots, Hp. Ep. 17.
ἀντεφοδεύω, Suid. ; turn and attack, of animals at bay, Ph. 2.354.
sub-procurator, Ephes. 2 No.28, cf. CIL 3.141954, al. ; ἀπὸ τῶν ἀ. ; a ramulariis, Gloss.
lay, inflict in turn upon, κακὰ πόλεσι Ph. 1.407 ; ἀντεποισόμεθα· ἀντεπενέγκω…, Hsch. (-επονησ- cod.). Pass., rush upon in turn, Ti.Locr. 102a.

make a counter-attack, Str. 5.2.2, cf. Max.Tyr. 18.9 ; τινί Plu. Them. 31.
make attempts to prove the contrary, Arist. Top. 160b10 ; τὰ ἀντεπιχειρούμενα controversial efforts to prove or disprove, S.E. M. 9.191.
εως, ἡ, a counter-attack, DH. 9.14.
v.l. ἀντεμπότευσις, εως, ἡ, Lat. compensatio, reputatio, Gloss.
aor. -ηράσθην, to be a rival in love, τινί τινος Luc. Musc. Enc. 10.
contribute one΄s share in turn ; — Pass., to be repaid, ὄμμασιν ἀλλοτρίοις AP 9.12 (Leon.).
οῦ, ὁ, rival in love, τινός Ar. Eq. 733 ; generally, rival, Pl. R. 521b, Arist. Rh. 1388a14 ; — fem. ἀντεράστρια, Gloss.

love in return, τῶν ἀντερώντων ἱμέρῳ πεπληγμένος A. Ag. 544 ; ἐρῶν ἀντερᾶται X. Smp. 8.3, cf. Bion Fr. 8.1 ; ἀντερᾶν τινός Luc. DMar. 1.5 ; ἀντερᾶσθαι ὑπό τινος Plu. Dio 16.
rival in love, τινί Id. 2.972d ; ἀ. τινί τινος rival one in love for…, E. Rh. 184 ; abs., τὸ ἀντερᾶν jealous love, Plu. Lyc. 18.
retaliate, τὰ αὐτά τινας ἀ. DC. Fr. 36.21.
compete with, τι in a thing, Posidipp. 3.1.
provoke in turn, τινὰ πρὸς μάχην Eust. 848.17.

set firmly against, χειρὶ χεῖρ’ ἀντερείσαις clasping hand in hand, Pi. P. 4.37 ; but ἄκναμπτον Ἥρᾳ μένος ἀν[τ]ερείδων Id. Pae. 6.87 ; ἀντέρειδε τοῖς Ἐρεχθείδαις δόρυ E. Supp. 702 ; ἀ. ξύλα [τῷ πύργῳ] set wooden stays or props against it, X. HG 5.2.5 ; ἀ. βάσιν plant it firm, S. Ph. 1403 ; λίθοι οἱ ἀντερείδοντες τὰς περιφερεῖς στέγας springers of a vault, Demetr. Eloc. 13.
intr., stand firm, resist pressure, offer resistance, opp. ὑπείκω, X. Cyr. 8.8.16, cf. Cyn. 10.16, Pl. Ti. 45c, Arist. MA 698b18, Epicur. Fr. 76 bis ; exert counter-pressure, θέναρι ἀ. Hp. Fract. 14 ; τὸ ὠθούμενον ἀ. ὅθεν ὠθεῖται offers resistance in the direction from which the pressure comes, Arist. Mech. 858a26 ; πρός or περί τι, Plu. 2.924d, 923e. metaph, exert mutual pressure, of contending politicians, Phld. Rh. 2.51 S. (dub.) ; simply, argue against, Sor. 2.57.

εως, ἡ, thrusting against, resistance, Hp. Art. 50 ; esp. the fulcrum or resistance used in reducing a dislocation, ib. 2 ; of joints, Arist. IA 705a14 ; λάμπειν ἀντερείσει τοῦ αἰθέρος by its resistance, Plu. Lys. 12 ; forward pressure, Ael. Tact. 18.8 ; repulsion, Plu. 2.396a, cf. Ph. 1.153, Plot. 4.3.26 (pl.).
Rhet., buttressing, mutual support, of clauses in a period, Demetr. Eloc. 12.
ατος, τό, prop, Hsch. s.v. στῆλαι.
ή, όν, of or for resistance, ἕζις Metop. ap. Stob. 3.1.115, Hierocl. p. 23A. ; κίνησις Simp. in Ph. 1046.12.
Att. ἀντερείττω, row against, πρὸς αὐτὸν τὸν ἄνεμον DC. 48.48.
strive against, contend, ταύροις Philostr. Her. 12b, cf. Hsch.
make equal in weight with, value equally with, c. gen., χρυσοῦ τε καὶ ἀργύρου ἀντερύσασθαι Thgn. 77 ; — Act., -ερύω pull in the opposite direction, Ep. impf. -ερύεσκε Nonn. D. 46.214.

fut. without any pres. in use ; pf. ἀντείρηκα S. Ant. 47 (cf. ἀντεῖπον) : — speak against, gainsay, S. l.c. ; τεθνάναι δ’ οὐκέτ’ ἀ. θεοῖς A. Ag. 539 ; τι πρός τινα Ar. Nu. 1079 ; πρός τι Ach. 701 ; τινί Pl. R. 580a ; — Pass., οὐδὲν ἀντειρήσεται no denial shall be given, S. Tr. 1184 ; τὰ ἀντειρημένα Gal. 5.477.

ωτος, ὁ, return-love, love-for-love, Pl. Phdr. 255d, Ach.Tat. 1.9, Them. Or. 24.305a.
Anteros, personified as a god who avenged slighted love, Paus. 1.30.1, etc. ; — but also (as it seems) a god who struggled against Ἔρως, Id. 6.23.5.
name of a gem, Plin. HN 37.123 (pl.).
question in turn, ἐρωτώμενος ἀντερωτᾷς; Pl. Euthd. 295b, cf. Aeschin. 3.226, Aen.Tact. 24.16, Plu. Cor. 18.
ἀντί<α>σον, ἄντικρυς ἐλθέ, Hsch.
Adv. pf. part. Pass. of ἀντιστρέφω.
part. (cf. τεταγών), holding aloft, prob. in ARh. 2.119.
ἀναγεγραμμένως, Hsch. (Perh. ἀντ’ ἔτεος ἀναγεγραμμένως (Dor. acc. pl.), = enrolled in the same year.)
τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἔτους (Lacon.), Hsch.
rival in distinction, Lyd. Mens. 1.28 (Pass.).
return a kindness, X. Mem. 2.6.4 ; ἀ. τοὺς εὖ ποιήσαντας Arist. Rh. Al. 1422a32.
ατος, τό, kindness returned, Hsch. s.v. ἀνθυπούργησον.
ου, ὁ, one who returns kindnesses, Asp. in EN 113.14, Sch. ARh. 2.321.
ή, όν, disposed to return kindnesses, Arist. EN 1124b11.
ζώνη south temperate zone, Cleom. 1.2, Stoic. 2.195.
wish well in return, τινί X. Cyr. 8.3.49 (divisim).

and ἀντευποιέω are by recent edd. written divisim ἀντ’ εὖ π. (v. Pl. Grg. 520e, X. An. 5.55.21, D. 20.124), on the ground that εὖ never enters into direct composition with Verbs, v. εὖ fin. ; but ἀντευποιεῖν is read in Arist. EN 1179a28, Rh. 1374a24.
= ἀντ’ εὖ π., Arist. EN 1179a28, Rh. 1374a24.
ἡ, requital of benefits, Mich. in EN 465.27.
ατος, τό, the opposite of joy, Agatho 30.
one must give thanks in turn, Porph. Abst. 2.37.
entertain in return, Ph. 2.139, Philostr. VS 2.5.3, Ael. NA 9.45, 15.7 ; as f.l. for ἀνταφ-, Pl. Ti. 17b.
find out against, J. AJ 10.8.1.
aor. inf. -ησθῆναι, exult over in turn, Ph. 2.313.
appoint against one, στρατηγούς τισι Aristid. 1.173J.
go forth to meet, Suid.
Pass., to be furnished instead of provisions ; metaph in J. AJ 15.9.1.
check, verify, SIG 1023.89 (Cos).
rush against, attack, Hld. 8.16 ; abs., Ph. 2.122.
anchor over against the enemy, Plu. Alc. 36.
εως, ἡ, rushing against, attack, Ph. 2.31, Hld. l.c.

or ἀντίσχω, fut. ἀνθέξω, part. ἀντισχήσων (in sense II) Lib. Ep. 33.2; aor. ἀντέσχον : — hold against, c. acc. et gen., χεῖρ’ ἀ. κρατός hold one΄s hand against one΄s head so as to shade the eyes, S. OC 1651 ; c. dat., ὄμμασι δ’ ἀντίσχοις (-έχοις codd.) τάνδ’ αἴγλαν may΄st thou keep this sunlight upon his eyes, Id. Ph. 830 (lyr.) ; τοὺς χαλινοὺς τῶν ἵππων Hdn. 5.6.7. c. dat., hold out against, withstand, Ἀρπάγῳ Hdt. 1.175, cf. 8.68. β’ ; τοῖς δικαίοις S. Fr. 78 ; τῇ ταλαιπωρίᾳ Th. 2.49 ; πρός τινα Id. 6.22 ; πρὸς τοὺς καμάτους Hdn. 3.6.10, etc. ; c. acc., endure, ἀντέχομεν καμάτους AP 9.299 (Phil.) ; but in Th. 8.63 ἀ. τὰ τοῦ πολέμου rather belongs to the next signf., hold out as regards the war ; so πολλὰ ἀ. ib. 86.
hold out, endure, c. part., ἡ Ἄζωτος… ἐπὶ πλεῖστον χρόνον πολιορκουμένη ἀντέσχε Hdt. 2.157, cf. 5.115, Th. 2.70 ; μηκέτι ἀντέχωσι τῷ πόνῳ διϊστάμενοι Pl. Ti. 81d ; πολλάκις γιγνομένην ψυχὴν ἀντέχειν last through several states of existence, Id. Phd. 88a. abs., hold out, stand one΄s ground, Hdt. 8.16, A. Pers. 413, etc. ; πῶς δύσμορος ἀντέχει; S. Ph. 176 (lyr.) ; νόσημα ἀντίσχει τὸν αἰῶνα πάντα Hp. Fract. 11 ; ἔστ’ ἂν αἰὼν ἀντέχῃ E. Alc. 337 ; βραχὺν χρόνον D. 2.10 ; ἀ. ἐπὶ πολύ, ἐπί πλέον, Th. 1.7, 65 ; ἀ. ἐλπίσιν in hope, DS. 2.26 ; ἀ. περί τινος X. HG 2.2.16 ; peculiarly, ἀ. μὴ ὑπακοῦσαι I hold out against…, refuse…, Plu. 2.708a. of the rivers drunk by the Persian army, hold out, suffice, Hdt. 7.196, cf. A. Pers. 413 (in full ἀ. ῥέεθρον Hdt. 7.58 ; ἀ. ὕδωρ παρέχων ib. 108) ; so ἀντέχει ὁ σῖτος Th. 1.65.
extend, reach, ἐς ὅσον ἡ ἐπιστήμη ἀ. Id. 6.69 ; prevail, διὰ τὴν λῃστείαν ἐπὶ πολὺ ἀντίσχουσαν 1.7.
Med., hold before one against something, c. acc. et gen., ἀντίσχεσθε τραπέζας ἰῶν hold out the tables against the arrows, Od. 22.74. c. gen. only, hold on by, cling to, ἐκείνου τῆς χειρός Hdt. 2.121. εʹ; πέπλων E. Tr. 750, cf. Ion 1404 ; τῶν θυρῶν Ar. Lys. 161 ; metaph, ἀ. τῶν ὄχθων cling to the banks, keep close to them, Hdt. 9.56 ; ἀ. Ἡρακλέος cleave to Hercules, i.e. worship him above all, Pi. N. 1.33 ; ἀ. τῆς ἀρετῆς, Lat. adhaerere virtuti, Hdt. 1.134 ; ἀ. τοῦ πολέμου Id. 7.53 ; τοῦ κέρδους S. Fr. 354 ; τῆς θαλάσσης Th. 1.13 ; σωτηρίας Lys. 33.6 ; τῆς ἀληθείας Pl. Phlb. 58e, cf. R. 600d, al. ; τῶν παραδεδομένων μύθων Arist. Po. 1451b24 ; τῆς ἐλευθερίας Decr. ap. D. 18.185 ; τῶν δικαίων POxy. 1203.30 (i AD). B.
c. gen. pers., care for, support, 1 Ep. Thess. 5.14. abs., αὐτὸς ἀντέχου S. Ph. 893, cf. Ar. Ach. 1121. c. dupl. gen. pers. et rei, ἀνθέξεταί σου τῶν πατρῴων χρημάτων will lay claim to the property from you, dispute it with you, Ar. Av. 1658.
resist, Pl. R. 574b ; φονεῦσαι τοὺς ἀντεχομένους DS. 4.49.
adhere, Arist. HA 583a18 ; Medic., of constipation, γαστὴρ ἀντίσχετο Hp. Epid. 4.20 ; γαστρὸς ἀντεχομένης ib. 17.
*ἀντήδην, Adv. in supplication, Hsch. (-δης cod.). ◊ read ἀντηδίς (Suppl.).
Adv. in supplication, Hsch.
δῶρον ἱκέσιον, Hsch.
Dor. ἀντάεις, εσσα, εν, (< ἄντα) hostile, Pi. P. 9.93.
ἡ, (ἄντομαι ΙΙ) prayer — a word preserved by Hsch. (ἄντῃσι (cod. ἀντήσει)· λιτανείαις, ἀντήσεσι), and restored by Herm. for λιταῖς (metri gr.) in S. El. 139 (dub.).

ον, (< ἀντί, ἥλιος) opposite the sun, i.e. looking east, S. Aj. 805, E. Ion 1550 ; δαίμονες ἀντήλιοι statues of gods which stood in the sun before the house-door, A. Ag. 519, cf. E. Fr. 538. of the moon, reflecting the sun΄s rays, AB 403 (ἀνθ-), cf. Suid. ; hence metaph, imitation, reflection, Theopomp.Hist. 367 (ἀνθ-). ἀντήλια, τά, = παρήλια, parhelia, Suid., cf. Men. 511.
screens or parasols, Eust. 1281.3 ; also, blinkers on horses’ bridles, Poll. 10.54 (ἀνθ-), Eust. 1562.39. — The Ion. form ἀντήλιος is always used in Trag. ; ἀνθήλιος first in Theopomp. l.c., cf. Ph. 1.656, Placit. 3.6.
όν, Ep. for ἀνταμοιβός, corresponding, Call. Del. 52.

Ep. Adv., (< ἀντί) against, over against, οὔ μιν ἔγωγε φεύξομαι… ἀλλὰ μάλ’ ἄ. στήσομαι I will confront him, Il. 18.307, cf. 11.590 ; ὁμοιωθήμεναι ἄ. match himself openly against me, 1.187, Od. 3.120 ; so πειρηθήμεναι ἄ. 8.213 ; more rarely with Verbs of motion, μηδ’ ἔα ἄ. ἔρχεσθαι straightforwards, opp. πάλιν τρέπε, 11.8.399 ; also ἄ. βαλλομένων in front, 12.152 ; οὐδέ τις ἔτλη ἄ. εἰσιδέειν look him in the face, 19.15, cf. 24.223 ; ἄ. λοέσσομαι will bathe before all, openly, Od. 6.221, cf. 8.158 ; ἀγαπαζέμεν ἄ. greet in the face of all, Il. 24.464 ; νείκεσέτ’ ἄ. 10.158 ; ὅς μ, eἴreai ἄ. 15.247 ; - θεῷ ἐναλίγκιος ἄ. like a god in presence, Od. 2.5, 4.310 ; χελιδόνι εἰκέλη ἄ. 22.240 ; cf. ἄντα. as Prep. c. gen., only in late Ep., as Nic. Th. 474, Opp. C. 3.210.
ορος, ὁ, ἡ, (< ἀνήρ) instead of a man, σποδὸς ἀ. dust for men, A. Ag. 442. — In Il. as pr. n.
row against or on the opposite side to another, EM 112.40.
ου, ὁ, (< ἐρέτης) properly, one who rows against another, cf. AB 411 ; generally, opponent, adversary, A. Th. 284, 595 ; ἀ. δορός τινι ib. 997 (lyr.).

Dor. ἀντάρης, ες, poet. Adj. set over against, opposite, λαβεῖν τινὰ ἀντήρη meet face to face in battle, E. Ph. 754, cf. 1367 ; ἀντήρεις στέρνων πληγάς blows on the breast, S. El. 89 ; c. gen., Φοινίκας ἀ. χώρα over against, facing it, E. Tr. 221 (lyr.) ; c. dat., ἀ. τινί opposite to a thing, Id. IA 224 ; ἀ. ὄψεσι, of the bat, hostile to, S. Fr. 747 (lyr.).

τό, Dim. of ἀντηρίς, stanchion supporting the base of a torsion-engine, Hero Bel. 89.4.
support, base, Milet.7 p. 60 (ii BC), Haussoullier Cinquantenaire de l΄École des Hautes Études p. 89 (ii BC).
στήμων, καὶ κανὼν ὁ προσκείμενος τῇ θύρᾳ, Hsch.

ίδος, ἡ, prop, stay, support, E. Fr. 1111 ; pl., Plb. 8.4.6 ; stanchion or strut in torsion-engines, Ph.Mech. Bel. 76.16, Hero Bel. 101.9 ; ἀρκύων X. Cyn. 10.7 ; in Th. 7.36 ἀντηρίδες are stay-beams fixed inside a ship΄s bow, and projecting beyond it, so as to support and strengthen the ἐπωτίδες. = θυρίς, window, Suid. ; — and in E. Rh. 785 it must mean nostrils, if it be the right reading. [ιδος E. ll. cc. ; hence ἀντήρειδες in Apollod. Poliorc. 178.4, Hero Bel. 101.9, is wrong ; so ἀντηρείδιον ib. 89.4 is f.l. for ἀντηρίδιον as Inscrr. show.] (-ηριδ = -εριδ-, weak form of stem of ἐρείδω (cf. ἔρις).)
εως, ἡ, entreaty, prayer, Hsch.
εως, ἡ, confronting, κατ’ ἄντηστιν θεμένη Od. 20.387.

Dor. ἀνταχέω Theoc. Ep. 4.11 (Scal.) : — sing in answer, παιᾶνα θεῷ E. Alc. 423 ; ἀντάχησ’ ἂν ὕμνον ἀρσένων γέννᾳ would have sung a song in answer to…, Id. Med. 426. abs., sound responsively, of a musical string, Arist. Pr. 919b16 ; of bronze vessels, Aen.Tact. 37.7, Plb. 22.11.12 ; resound, Hp. Morb. 4.56, cf. Carn. 18, Luc. VH 1.38 ; echo, φωναῖς ἀ. Plu. 2.414c.
shout in opposition, Id. Mar. 19, cf. J. BJ 2.19.8, Them. Or. 21.255d contradict, Plu. 2.925e, cf. 1000c.
ατος, τό, echo, Sch. Philostr. Her. 19.12.
εως, ἡ, a re-echoing, Plu. 2.589d.
ον, sounding in response, ἁρμονία Ph. 1.312, 2.485.

Prep. governing gen. ; — orig. sense, over against. (Cf. Skt. ánti ΄opposite΄, ΄facing΄, Lat. ante, etc.)
USAGE : of Place, opposite, over against, formerly quoted from several places of Hom., as Il. 21.481 ἀντὶ ἐμεῖο (where now ἀντί’ ἐμεῖο, i.e. ἀντία) Τρώων ἄνθ’ ἑκατόν (i.e. ἄντα) 8.233 ; so ἄντ’ Αἴαντος (i.e. ἄντα) 15.415, cf. Od. 4.115, Hes. Op. 727 ; but ἀντί is so used in X. An. 4.7.6, IG 2.835c-l68 ; αἱ ὀπαὶ αἱ γιγνόμεναι ἀ. τόρμων mortises facing tenons, Hero Bel. 97.5 ; ἀντὶ μαιτύρων in the presence of witnesses, Leg. Gort. 1.40 ; ἀντὶ τῆς ὄψεως ἡμῶν Eudox. Ars 18.
of Time, ἀντὶ νυκτός the same night, SIG 1025.43 (Cos) ; ἀντὶ ϝέτεος GDI 2561 A 45 (Delph.) ; ἀντ’ ἐνιαυτοῦ IG 5(2).266.8 (Mantinea, i BC) ; ἀνθ’ ἡμέρας· δι’ ὅλης τῆς ἡμέρας, Hsch. ; cf. ἀντετοῦς.
instead, in the place of, Ἕκτορος ἀντὶ πεφάσθαι Il. 24.254 ; ἀντὶ γάμοιο τάφον Od. 20.307 ; so later πολέμιος ἀντὶ φίλου καταστῆναι Hdt. 1.87 ; ἀντὶ ἡμέρης νὺξ ἐγένετο Id. 7.37 ; ἀντὶ φωτῶν σποδός A. Ag. 434 ; τὸν πόλεμον ἀντ’ εἰρήνης μεταλαμβάνειν Th. 1.120, cf. 4.20, 7.75 ; βασιλεύειν ἀντί τινος X. An. 1.1.4 ; also ἀντὶ ἄρχεσθαι ὑπ’ ἄλλων ἄρχειν ἁπάντων Hdt. 1.210, cf. 6.32, 7.170 (where the usual constr. would be ἀντὶ τοῦ ἄρχεσθαι, cf. Th. 7.28, X. Cyr. 6.2.19, etc.) ; ὀργίλοι ἀντὶ θυμοειδοῦς γεγένηνται Pl. R. 411c ; sts. used elliptically, ἦ ΄τολμήσατ’ ἀντ’ ἐμοῦ δοῦναί τινι; i.e. ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐμοὶ δοῦναι, S. Ph. 369, cf. OC 448, Ar. Av. 58. in Hom. often to denote equivalence, ἀντί νυ πολλῶν λαῶν ἐστιν ἀνήρ he is as good as many men, Il. 9.116 ; ἀντὶ κασιγνήτου ξεῖνος… τέτυκται a guest is as much as a brother, Od. 8.546 ; ἀντί τοί εἰμ’ ἱκέταο I am as a suppliant, Il. 21.75, cf. 8.163 ; so later τοῦτό σφι ἀντὶ λουτροῦ ἐστί serves as a bath, Hdt. 4.75 ; ὑπάρχειν ἀντὶ τῶν ἔνδον to be as hostages for…, Th. 2.5 ; δουλεύειν ἀντὶ ἀργυρωνήτων just like bought slaves, D. 17.3 ; ἀντὶ [πλεύμονος] βράγχια Arist. PA 669a4. to denote exchange, at the price of, in return for, σοὶ δὲ θεοὶ τῶνδ’ ἀντὶ χάριν… δοῖεν Il. 23.650 ; νῆσον ἀντὶ χρημάτων παρέλαβον for money paid, Hdt. 3.59 ; ἀντ’ ἀργυρίου ἀλλάξασθαι Pl. R. 371d ; ἀμείβειν τι ἀντί τινος Pi. P. 4.17, cf. E. Or. 646, 651 ; ἀντὶ ποίας εὐεργεσίας; Lys. 6.40, etc. ; τί δ’ ἐστὶν ἀνθ’ οὗ… ; S. Ant. 237 ; ὄνειδος ἀνθ’ ὅτου Id. OC 967 ; δοίην ἀντ’ ἀνιῶν ἀνίας grief for grief, Thgn. 344 ; ἀντ’ ἀγαθῶν ἀγαθοῖσι βρύοις A. Supp. 966 ; — hence ἀνθ’ ὧν wherefore, A. Pr. 31, S. OT 264, Th. 6.83, Ev. Luc. 12.3 ; ἀντὶ τούτου therefore, Ep. Eph. 5.31 ; but ἀνθ’ ὧν also for ἀντὶ τούτων ὄτι…, because, S. Ant. 1068, Ar. Pl. 434 ; ἀντὶ τοῦ; wherefore? why? S. OT 1021 ; also ἀνθ’ ὧν ὅτι ἦτε… instead of being as you were…, LXX De. 28.62.
for the sake of, Pl. Mx. 237a, Arist. EN 1110a21 ; with Verbs of entreaty, like πρός c. gen., ἀντὶ παίδων ἱκετεύομέν σε S. OC 1326. to mark comparison, ἓν ἀνθ’ ἑνός one set against the other, compared with it, Pl. R. 331b, Lg. 705b ; χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος, i.e. ever-increasing grace, Ev. Jo. 1.16 ; in preference to, ἀφνεὸν βούλεται ἀντ’ ἀγαθοῦ Thgn. 188 ; ἀντὶ αὐλοῦ καὶ ἀντὶ κιθάρας ὁ ἦχος ἀκούεται Demetr. Eloc. 71 ; αἱρεῖσθαί τι ἀντί τινος Isoc. 9.3, D. 1.1, cf. X. Lac. 9.1 ; even after Comparatives, πλέον ἀντὶ σοῦ S. Tr. 577 ; μείζον’ ὅστις ἀντὶ τῆς αὑτοῦ πάτρας φίλον νομίζει Id. Ant. 182 ; so (esp. after a neg.) ἄλλος ἀντ’ ἐμοῦ A. Pr. 467, S. Aj. 444, Ar. Nu. 653 ; δόξαν ἀντὶ τοῦ ζῆν ἠγαπηκώς Plu. Alex. 42.
POSITION ; ἀντί rarely follows its case, as in Il. 23.650, A. Ag. 1277, Ig 5(1).1119 (Geronthrae, iv BC), AP 7.715 (Leon.) ; but the Gramm. hold that it never suffers anastrophe.
IN COMPOS. it signifies,
over against, opposite, as ἀντιβαίνω, ἀντίπορος.
against, in opposition to, as ἀντιλέγω, ἀντίβιος.
one against another, mutually, as ἀντιδεξιόομαι.
in return, as ἀντιβοηθέω.
instead of, as ἀντιβασιλεύς, ἀνθύπατος.
equal to, like, as ἀντίθεος, ἀντίπαις, ἀντίδουλος.
corresponding, counter, as ἀντίφορτος, ἀντίτυπος.
v. sub ἀντίος.

impf. ἀντίαζον Hdt. 1.166 (but ὑπηντίαζον 4.121), ἠντίαζον (ὑπ-) X. An. 6.5.27, etc. ; fut. ἀντιάσω [α] ; Dor. -άξω (v. infr.) ; aor. ἠντίασα Hdt. 4.80, 9.6 ; but these two tenses belong also to ἀντιάω ; (< ἀντί) :
meet face to face ; c. acc. pers., encounter, whether as friend or foe, τὸν ἐπιόντα Id. 4.118, cf. 2.141, 4.80, etc. ; ἀ. [τινὰ] ἐς τόπον Hdt. 1.166, cf. 9.6 ; πατέρ’ ἀντιάσασα πρὸς… πόρθμευμα A. Ag. 1557 ; abs., κόρος… βαρὺς ἀντιάσαι Pi. N. 10.20 ; μολπὰ πρὸς κάλαμον ἀντιάξει song shall answer to the pipe, Id. O. 10 (11).84.
approach as suppliants, ἀ. τινὰ δώροισι Hdt. 1.105 ; hence simply, entreat, supplicate, Ἄρεα ἀντιάζω S. OT 192 ; καί σ’ ἀντιάζω πρὸς… Διός Id. Aj. 492, cf. E. Andr. 572, etc. ; freq. with acc. omitted, ἀλλ’ ἀντιάζω S. El. 1009, cf. Ph. 809, E. Alc. 400 ; βᾶθι καὶ ἀντίασον γονάτων entreat [her] by her knees, Id. Supp. 272. = ἀντιάω II, ἀντάω, c. dat. pers. et acc. rei, ὅταν θεοὶ… Γιγάντεσσιν μάχαν ἀντιάζωσιν in fight, Pi. N. 1.68. — This Verb is never used in correct Att. Prose.

ἡ, (< ἀντί, ἀνήρ), fem. form of a masc. in -άνωρ or -ήνωρ ; in Il. always as epith. of the Amazons, a match for men, 3.189, 6.186, etc. ; so of Athena, Coluth. 170. in Pi. O. 12.16 στάσις ἀντιάνειρα faction wherein man is set against man.
άδος, ἡ, tonsil, mostly in pl., Hp. Morb. 2.11 and 30 ; esp. when inflamed, Cels. 7.12, Gal. 7.263 ; cf. παρίσθμια.
οῦ, ὁ, Anti-Atticist, title of grammatical work, AB 77.
ου, ὁ, a stone like an agate, dub. in Orph. L. 637 (Abel).
cry or call against, Theoc. Ep. 4.11 codd. (ἀνταχεῦσι Scal.), ARh. 2.828.
= ἀντιαχέω, Orph. A. 828 ; ἀμοιβήδην ἀντίαχεν ARh. 4.76.
Adv. going against, opposite, ἀ. ὠθεῖν Plu. 2.381a.
go against, the contrary way, Phot. s.v. ῥαβάττειν.
obvagio, Gloss.

fut. -βήσομαι, go against, withstand, resist, c. dat., Hdt. 5.40, A. Pr. 236, Decr. ap. D. 18.186, etc. ; πλευραῖσιν ἀντιβᾶσα having set her foot against…, E.
