ον, not loving money, Inscr.Prien. 137.5 (ii BC), DS. 9.11, 1 Ep. Ti. 3.3, Ep. Hebr. 13.5, Sor. 1.4, POxy. 33 ii 11 (ii AD). Adv. -ρως IG2². 1343.25 (i BC), SIG 708.17 (Istropolis, ii BC).
brighten, cheer, Phld. Mus. p. 84 K.
= ἀφιλαρόω, in Pass., have a cheerful expression, Stoic. 3.43.
appease, θυμόν Pl. Lg. 873a ; ἀφειλαξόμενον (sc. the gods) Polystr. p. 9 W.
ον, not showing self-love, Plu. 2.542b.
Adv. with no disposition towards enmity, Sch. Od. 8.77.
ον, not liking sensuality, Ph. 2.458, M.Ant 5.5.
καθαρός, ὑγιής, ὁλόκληρος, Hsch.
ον, unloved, S. OC 1702 (lyr.), Phld. D. 1.1.
ἡ, want of friends, Arist. EN 1115a11, Rh. 1386a9, Phld. Oec. p. 67J., Plu. Sol. 7.
ον, not to be made a friend of or reconciled, Hsch. s.v. ἀσύμβατον.
to be free from ambition, prob. in Phld. Vit. p. 7J.
ον, free from conceit or ambition, Phld. Rh. 2.273S., Lib. p. 42 O. ; τὸ ἀ. Cic. Att. 2.17.2, Ph. 2.458.
ον, gen. ονος, unmerciful, Hsch.
[pap. ἀφι<λοκα>λοκαγαθία] ἡ, dishonesty, POxy. 33 ii 13 (ii AD).
ον, without adornment, δόμος Procl. ad Hes. Op. 746, cf. Eust. 669.41.
ἡ, character of the ἀφιλόκαλος, Ath. 1.3a (cf. Eup. 366).
ον, without love for beauty or honour, Plu. 2.672e, Gal. 5.39.
ον, without love for learning lilerature, Plu. 2.673a.
ον, = ἀφιλόνεικος, Hdn. Epim. 177.
ον, not fond of strife, Arist. VV 1250a43, 1251a15, Andronic. Rhod. p. 575 M., Ph. 2.5 ; ἡγεμονία ib. 555. Adv. -κως, παραχωρεῖν τινός τινι Plb. 21.20.1, cf. Ph. 1.324, al., Luc. Symp. 37.
ον, inhospitable, Eust. 1733.20.
ἡ, contempt for wealth, Plu. Comp. Lys. Sull. 3.
ον, disliking work, Plb. 12.27.4 (Comp.).
ἡ, want of ambition, Men. Prot. p. 90 D.

ον, of persons, friendless, A. Ch. 295, S. El. 819, Pl. Lg. 730c, R. 580a ; ἄ. ἔρημον ἄπολιν S. Ph. 1018 ; ἄκλαυτος ἄ. Id. Ant. 876 (lyr.) ; c. gen., ἄ. φίλων E. Hel. 524 (lyr.) ; τὸ ἄ. Ph. 2.662. of persons and things, unfriendly, hateful, A. Th. 522, S. OC 186 ; ἄφιλα παρ’ ἀφίλοις ἔπεσε… Ἀτρείδαις Id. Aj. 620 ; λίαν ἄφιλον φαίνεται Arist. EN 1101a23 ; unsociable, γῆρας S. OC 1237 ; perh., c. gen., hostile to, ἀσφαλείας Phld. Lib. p. 36O. ; τὸ λαθραιοπραγεῖν ἀφιλώτατον ib. p. 20 O., cf. Carneisc. Herc. 1027.16. Adv. -λως in unfriendly manner, A. Ag. 805.

ον, not versed in philosophy, ὄχλος DH. 2.20, Phld. Herc. 1005.11.
without philosophical significance, Arg. Sch. Od. 1.
ἡ, contempt for philosophy, Pl. Def. 415e.

ον, of persons, without taste for philosophy, Pl. Sph. 259e, Ph. Fr. 35 H. ; γένος Pl. Ti. 73a ; σνγγραφεύς unphilosophical, Plb. 12.25.6. of conditions, unphilosophic, δίαιτα Pl. Phdr. 256c ; ἀ. τήρησις S.E. M. 11.165.
ον, without ears of corn, starving, πενία AP 6.40.8 (Maced.).
ἡ, absence of natural affection, implied in punning phrase of Timagenes, ἡ πρὸς τὰ ἔκγονα φιλοστοργία (< ἔκγον’ ἀ.) Plu. 2.634f.
ον, without natural affection, Plu. 2.140d.
ἡ, want of due ambition, Arist. EN 1125b22.

ον, lacking in ambition, Is. 7.35, Lycurg. 69, Arist. EN 1107b29 ; Sup., Plb. 6.48.8 ; βίος ἀ. εἰς δόξαν Inscr.Prien. 112.11, cf. Eun. VS p. 491 B. Adv. -μως Plb. 12.23.8 ; πρὸς πολίτας ζῆν Plu. 2.525d ; but also, without fear or favour, impartial, IG 9(2).517.34 (Epist. Philipp.). simply, indifferent, πρὸς κάλλος J. AJ 2.9.6. Adv. -μως lukewarmly, PPetr. 2 p. 5. of things, not honourable, paltry, ἡ ἀπὸ μικρῶν δόξα ἀ. Plu. 2.35a.
ἡ, contempt for riches, Plu. Comp. Ag. Gracch. 1, Socr. Ep. 5.2 ; — hence Adj. ἀφιλοχρήματος, ον, Ph. 2.458, Eun. Hist. p. 243 D.
v. ἀφιλοχρηματία.
ον, not cowardly, prob. in Plu. 2.761c.
(< ἱμάτιον) strip of clothing, Suid.
εως, ἡ, an operation connected with the manufacture of vegetable oils, PPetr. 3 p. 315.

εως, Ion. ἄπιξις, ιος, ἡ (< ἀφικνέομαι) : — arrival, Hdt. 1.69, al. ; τὴν ἀπὸ Κορίνθου ἄ. arrival from C., Id. 5.92. ζ’ ; ἐς Θήβας Id. 9.17 ; ἄ. ἐπὶ Σαρπηδονίης ἄκρης ποιεῖσθαι Id. 7.58 ; μέρος αὐτῆς ἀπίξιος παρὰ τὸν μάγον her turn for going in to him, Id. 3.69, cf. Pl. Ep. 337e, Aristeas 173, J. Ap. 1.18, etc. ; ἄ. εἰς τοὺς πολεμίους ποιησάμενος D. 5.8 ; ἄ. εἰς Κύπρον Isoc. 9.53 ; ἡ ἐνθάδε ἄ. Hdt. 3.145, Lys. 2.26 ; ἡ οἴκαδε ἄ. home again, D. Ep. 1.2, 3.39.
departure, J. AJ 2.2.4, Act. Ap. 20.29. = ἱκεσία, A. Supp. 483.
aor. -ασάμην Hld. 7.29, etc. : — ride off or away, Plb. 29.6.18, Str. 7.2.1, J. AJ 14.13.5, Plu. Aem. 19, Luc. Tox. 50.
